## 2026-07-28 — illumos RISC-V R-P4: SMP + cyclic clock + PLIC + high-VA hat (DONE)


Advanced the first illumos RISC-V (riscv64) port from **R-P3** (trap + Sv39
paging + one-shot timer) to **R-P4**: the four MD pieces needed before genunix,
all verified on `qemu-system-riscv64 -machine virt -smp 4` under OpenSBI
(fw v1.5.1 / SBI v2.0).

### Four sub-gates — ALL PASS (verbatim console in artifacts/riscv-port/rp4/rp4-boot.log)

1. **SMP secondary hart bringup (SBI HSM): YES — 3 secondaries.** Boot hart
   probes harts via `sbi_hart_get_status`, starts each STOPPED secondary via
   `sbi_hart_start(h, PA(_secondary_start), stacktop)`. Each secondary adopts a
   per-cpu stack, installs `stvec`, loads the SHARED `kernel_satp`, and reports
   `hart N online`. `secondaries started=3 online-reported=3`; `cpus online: 4
   (1 boot + 3 secondary)`.
2. **Cyclic/periodic clock: YES.** Reworked timer.c from one-shot to periodic
   at HZ=100 (10 ms period, self-rearming in `timer_intr`), `gethrtime` scales
   the `time` CSR (10 MHz) to ns. `[clock] 10 ticks, hrtime=239057900 ns
   (elapsed 100235800 ns)` — exactly 100 Hz; status line shows 11 ticks (kept
   ticking during the banner = genuinely periodic, not one-shot).
3. **PLIC external interrupts: YES.** New plic.c (init/enable/claim/complete);
   `trap()` routes `IRQ_S_EXT` → `plic_extintr()`. Self-test enables the
   NS16550A UART source (IRQ 10) + `SIE.SEIE`, triggers via THRE (non-interactive),
   takes the external interrupt, claims + completes. `[plic] IRQ 0xa claimed ...
   external IRQ 0xa claimed + completed via PLIC`.
4. **Real high-VA hat: YES.** Added a bump phys page allocator over RAM above
   the kernel, `hat_kmap_page` (4 KiB map via the full 3-level Sv39 walk), and
   mapped a fresh page at canonical `KERNELBASE=0xffffffc000000000`, wrote a
   signature through the high VA + read it back both ways: `wrote
   0x5041474544554d50 ... MATCH -> high-VA translation verified`.

### Sources (src/riscv/uts/)
- **new:** `plic.c` (PLIC driver + external-IRQ path + self-test).
- **updated:** `sbi.c`/`sbi.h` (SBI HSM: `sbi_hart_start`/`sbi_hart_get_status`,
  EID 0x48534D), `locore.S` (`_secondary_start` + `kernel_satp` + per-cpu stack
  pool), `riscv_regs.h` (`KERNELBASE`, CLINT/PLIC/UART bases), `hat_riscv.c`
  (publish `kernel_satp`; bump allocator `hat_phys_init`/`hat_palloc`;
  `hat_kmap_page`; `hat_highva_prove`; boot table pool 4→6), `timer.c` (periodic
  clock + `gethrtime`), `trap.c` (`IRQ_S_EXT` → `plic_extintr`), `main.c`
  (`secondary_main`, `start_secondaries`, `cpu_online[]`, console spinlock,
  R-P4 mlsetup sequence + status), `build-unix.sh` (`plic.c` + `-smp 4`).

### One bug found + fixed during bringup
SMP online-count race: the boot hart's wait loop used `ncpu_online >= started+1`
(wrongly counting the boot hart in `ncpu_online`, which only counts secondaries)
with too small a spin bound, so it snapshotted the count mid-arrival and reported
2/3. Fixed: `ncpu_online` counts secondaries only, wait on `>= started` with an
acquire fence + generous bound; all 3 now report reliably. Also serialized all
multi-hart console output through the `console_lock` (was interleaving:
`[s[msp]mp]`).

### Deliberate scope ceilings (R-P5 upgrade paths, documented in design §R-P4.5)
one-way bump allocator (no free, RAM cap is a 128 MiB constant not DTB-probed);
periodic heartbeat only (no cyclic wheel/callouts/TOD); PLIC UART source quiesced
after the proof (console still SBI DBCN polled); secondaries park in `wfi` (no
per-cpu dispatch/idle, no IPI yet); hat has no ASIDs/`hat_unload`/VA allocator.

### Build / env
nixpkgs `pkgsCross.riscv64-embedded` (riscv64-none-elf gcc 14.3.0, binutils
2.44), freestanding `-mcmodel=medany`; qemu 10.1.5 on the dev box. **Every qemu
run was `timeout`-wrapped + detached** (nohup→log, sleep+check+kill); no
foreground-wait, no wedge; stray-qemu confirmed gone after each run. **No
ponytail** (genuine kernel port work, full rigor). **No git commit.**

Artifacts: `artifacts/riscv-port/rp4/` (rp4-boot.log, unix, unix.disasm,
unix.sections). Design: `docs/design-riscv-port.md` §R-P4 (SMP/clock/PLIC/hat
contracts for R-P5 genunix). Sources: `src/riscv/uts/`.

### R-P5 (genunix) — exact next step
FDT `/memory` parse → real `page_t`/freelists + a kernel VA allocator over the
`KERNELBASE` high range + `kmem` slab; the cyclic wheel/callouts on the R-P4
periodic clock; turn the secondary `wfi` park into per-cpu idle threads + the
dispatcher (SBI IPI for cross-hart `sfence`/reschedule); a PLIC-driven NS16550A
console; then grow `mlsetup`'s boot `cpu_t` into the real `cpu_t[]` and have
`main()` call MI `startup()` toward mounting root.

### gnulib getlocalename_l fix — WORKED, unblocks the family
The wave-1 libunistring blocker: gnulib `localename-unsafe.c:51` declared
`extern char * getlocalename_l(int, locale_t)` but the illumos aarch64 sysroot
`locale.h:98` declares `const char *getlocalename_l(...)` → conflicting types.
**FIX:** patched all 3 bundled gnulib `.c` copies to `extern const char *`.
gettext then compiled clean past the conflict — **the family fix works for cross**
(same gnulib copy ships in libunistring + coreutils, so they're now unblocked too).
A SECOND, unrelated gnulib blocker then surfaced in gettext-tools:
`memset_explicit.c` calls `memset_s` under `HAVE_MEMSET_S=1` (the cross link-probe
sees the libc symbol) but `string.h` doesn't declare it → implicit-decl error.
**FIX:** configure with `ac_cv_func_memset_s=no` → portable volatile-memset path.
Both fixes together → gettext builds fully (libgettextlib/src/po, libtextstyle,
msgfmt, xgettext — all EM_AARCH64) and is published.

### TOOLCHAIN FIX discovered this wave (applies to ALL aarch64 cross builds)
The illumos aarch64 `ld` rejects **TLSDESC relocations**
(`R_AARCH64_TLSDESC_*: relocation not currently supported`) emitted by GCC's
default TLS dialect. First hit by gdbm (TLS in libgdbm). **FIX (now baked into the
driver + every custom job):** compile with `-mtls-dialect=trad` (traditional TLS
relocs link cleanly). Verified with a minimal `__thread` shared-lib testcase.

### Other transient failures (all fixed + rebuilt — see artifacts/aa-xbuild2/failures.txt)
- zlib: zlib.net URL 404 → github madler release tarball.
- lz4/zstd/openssl: Solaris `tar` exits nonzero on GNU pax_global_header (extraction
  still succeeds) → `|| true` after tar.
- xz: my invalid `--disable-shared=no` → removed; shared liblzma built.
- zstd: shared textrels → added `-fPIC`.
- openssl: no `solaris64-aarch64-gcc` target; `linux-aarch64` passes GNU
  `--version-script` (illumos ld rejects) → custom
  `Configurations/99-solaris-aarch64.conf` inheriting `solaris-common-gcc`

### gnulib getlocalename_l cross-fix — LANDED (unblocks the libunistring/gettext/coreutils family)
The illumos aarch64 sysroot `locale.h:98` declares `extern const char *getlocalename_l(int, locale_t);`
but gnulib's bundled `lib/localename-unsafe.c:51` declares `extern char * getlocalename_l(int, locale_t);`
→ conflicting-types → gmake dies at `config.h`. Fix (baked into `aa-xbuild3-driver.sh`):
`sed -E 's/extern[[:space:]]+char[[:space:]]*\*[[:space:]]*getlocalename_l/extern const char *getlocalename_l/'`
over every bundled `localename*.c` before configure. First attempt's sed missed the space
after `char *`; the corrected pattern matched and libunistring built clean (EM_AARCH64,
libunistring.so.5). This is the family unblock: libidn2 then built directly against it, and
gettext/coreutils can reuse the same driver patch.

### Cross-compile gotchas solved this wave
- **bdw-gc** `conflicting types for 'open'`: `os_dep.c` calls `open`/`fcntl` before including
  `<fcntl.h>` (implicit decl clashes with the real prototype). Fix: `CFLAGS+=-include fcntl.h`.
- **p11-kit** `ULONG_MAX undeclared` in rpc-server.c: missing `<limits.h>`. Fix: `-include limits.h`.
- **popt** `iconv` const-mismatch (sysroot `iconv(iconv_t, const char **, ...)` vs popt's `char **`):
  gcc-14 treats incompatible-pointer as a hard error. Fix: `-Wno-error=incompatible-pointer-types`.
- **libpsl** libtool chased a "moved" `//lib/libunistring.la` (store `.la` records `libdir=/lib`
  after `DESTDIR=/`). Fix: stage libidn2+libunistring into a writable prefix WITHOUT the `.la`
  files and rewrite the `.pc` prefixes; libpsl then linked via `-L<stage>/lib -lidn2 -lunistring`.

### Failures / deferrals (artifacts/aa-xbuild3/failures.txt)
- **libgpg-error-1.51 BUILD_FAIL** → mkheader emitted a *truncated* `src/gpg-error.h`
  (24 `#if` vs 22 `#endif`, ends mid-"Lock functions."). Root cause: libgpg-error assembles

  (both marked BLOCKED, not attempted).
- **snappy-1.2.1 / json-c-0.18 / libcbor-0.11.0 SKIP** → cmake-only (snappy also C++); no cmake
  on builder (`which cmake` → not found). Deferred to a wave with cmake staged.

## RISC-V R-P6 — the first illumos RISC-V kernel becomes a RUNNING OS


R-P6 advances the illumos riscv64 port from R-P5 (VM + scheduling seam) to a
device-driving, root-mounting, single-user-reaching OS. Built on the R-P5
MD->MI seam; ZERO regressions (SMP 4/4 harts + all R-P5 gates still pass). Sources
in `src/riscv/uts/`; boot artifacts in `artifacts/riscv-port/rp6/`.

New sources: `virtio.c`+`virtio.h` (virtio-mmio transport + split virtqueue),
`vioblk.c` (virtio-blk sector read = the DMA crux), `vionet.c` (virtio-net
TX/RX), `rootfs.c` (minimal vnode/vfs + mount-root + single-user seam);
`startup.c` gains `startup_root()`.

### R-P6 gates — REPORT

- **virtio-mmio discovery: YES (2 devices).** Scanned the qemu-virt window
  (0x10001000..0x10008000, 8 slots, IRQ=slot+1): found net@0x10007000 (dev-id
  1, v2, irq 7) + blk@0x10008000 (dev-id 2, v2, irq 8).
  `virtio-mmio: found 2 devices (net@0x0000000010007000, blk@0x0000000010008000)`
- **vioblk sector read: YES (the crux — DMA proven).**
  `vioblk: read sector 0 OK (512 bytes, MBR/magic=0x000000000000aa55, first8=534f4c4e49582d52)`
  — magic 0xaa55 (MBR sig) + first8 = ASCII "SOLNIX-R" read back off disk.img =
  virtio DMA + device I/O end-to-end via a split-ring request chain (poll-based
  completion).
- **root mounted: YES.**
  `root mounted (type=ramdisk, / has 5 entries)` (in-memory read-only root vfs:
  /etc /dev /sbin /var /tmp; root device recorded as the virtio-blk disk).
- **single-user reached: YES.**
  `[R-P6] root on /dev/dsk/c0t0d0 (virtio-blk), single-user reached` — kernel-thread
  init-analog prints the single-user banner + `#` prompt.
- **vionet: YES (TX).** `vionet: TX OK` — MAC 52:54:00:12:34:56 read from config,
  60-byte broadcast ARP transmitted, TX used-ring completion taken. RX
  best-effort, not seen in the headless poll window (slirp doesn't reply;
  honestly reported, not a driver failure).

### Key fix (root-caused, not symptom-patched)

qemu virtio-mmio defaults to the **legacy (v1)** transport (QueuePFN ABI), not
modern (v2, independent DESC/AVAIL/USED addresses). The first run's vioblk
"request timed out" — `-d guest_errors` showed `read/write ... in legacy mode`.
Fix at the boundary: `-global virtio-mmio.force-legacy=false` forces v2 so the
clean modern driver works; `virtq_setup` also now refuses a v1 device rather
than silently writing registers it ignores. After the flip, features flipped to
v2 (bit 32 VERSION_1 set) and the sector read completed first try.

### Exact stop + R-P7 next step

STOP: single-user seam reached (kernel-thread stub, S-mode). Root is the
in-memory ramdisk vfs; the virtio-blk disk is attached + proven readable but
NOT yet the backing store for `/`. No U-mode, no ELF exec, no interactive
console input, virtio completions are polled (not IRQ-driven).

R-P7 (userland/init + K1/K3): (1) grow the vnode/vfs into a real lookup/read
path + read a root FS image off vioblk so `/` is disk-backed; (2) U-mode entry
(sstatus.SPP=0) + ELF loader + per-process address spaces (user page tables +
curproc) + the `ecall` syscall path + `exec` of `/sbin/init`; (3) wire NS16550A
(or virtio-console) RX through the PLIC for an interactive single-user shell;
(4) IRQ-driven virtio via `plic_extintr` + per-cpu dispatch + clock-tick
preemption.

Confirmations: every qemu run timeout-wrapped + detached (nohup->log,
sleep+check+kill), NO foreground-wait, NO wedge, stray qemu confirmed gone after
each run ✓  deterministic on -smp 1 AND -smp 4 ✓  0 PANIC/MISMATCH, SMP intact
(4/4 harts) ✓  NO "ponytail" in any R-P6 source (used NOTE:) ✓  no git commit ✓


## 2026-07-28 — illumos RISC-V R-P7: USERLAND — U-mode + syscalls + ELF exec + interactive init (DONE)


**MILESTONE MET — the first illumos RISC-V system is USABLE: userland runs in
U-mode.** Advanced the port from **R-P6** (single-user seam, S-mode kernel-thread
stub) to **R-P7**: a per-process address space, a U/S trap-frame split, the
`ecall`-from-U syscall path, a static ELF64 loader, and `exec` of a real
`/sbin/init` that runs in **U-mode** and drives an **interactive console**
(read/write/exit syscalls), then cleanly exits back to the kernel.

All three R-P7 gates PASS deterministically; 0 PANIC / 0 MISMATCH; the kernel
continues its normal boot after init exits.

### Gates (verbatim console, `artifacts/riscv-port/rp7/rp7-boot.log`)

- **Gate 1 — U-mode + syscall path: YES.**
  ```
  [exec] switching to process address space (satp=0x8000000000087fed), 5 user pages mapped; entering U-mode
  hi
  U-mode syscall OK: write() from userland
  ```
  A fresh Sv39 root (per-process satp) is built, we `sret` to U-mode (SPP=0,
  SPIE=1, SUM=1), the userland blob does `ecall` (write), scause=8 traps to S,
  syscall.c dispatches, and the byte reaches the console — the U/S boundary and
  the syscall entry are proven.
- **Gate 2 — ELF loader: YES.**
  ```
  [elf]   PT_LOAD vaddr=0x00000000c0010000 filesz=426 memsz=426 perm=r-x
  exec: loaded /sbin/init (1 segments, entry 0x00000000c001002c)
  ```
  elf.c validates a static riscv64 ELF (EM_RISCV=243, ET_EXEC, ELFCLASS64 LSB),
  walks the program headers, maps each PT_LOAD into the user AS (filesz copied,
  memsz zero-filled, perms from p_flags), and returns e_entry.
- **Gate 3 — exec init + interactive console: YES.**
  ```
  [R-P7] userland /sbin/init running in U-mode; interactive console
  init> type chars (they echo); press 'q' to exit.
  init> Xy!q
  init: got 'q', exiting.

  [R-P7] userland process called exit(0)
  [exec] process exited, status 0; back in kernel
  ```
  /sbin/init (a hand-built static riscv64 ELF) runs in U-mode, `read(0)`s chars
  from the NS16550A console (polled), echoes them via `write(1)`, and `exit(0)`s
  on 'q'. The scripted input `Xy!` was echoed and `q` triggered the exit — the
  console is genuinely interactive. On exit the kernel switches back to the
  kernel satp and resumes; startup completes cleanly (no post-exit fault).

### What was written (src/riscv/uts/)

- `regs.h` — the `struct regs` trap frame, extracted from trap.c so the syscall
  / AS / exec paths share it (analog of sys/regset.h). Layout asserted against
  asm_frame.h in trap.c.
- `trap.S` (R-P7 U/S split) — on entry `csrrw sp, sscratch, sp` swaps to a
  kernel stack when trapping from U-mode (sscratch=kernel-stack-top in U, 0 in
  S); saves the user sp; on return restores sp from TF_SP (user sp for U,
  prior kernel sp for S — one path, correct for both) and sets sscratch for the
  next trap. New `usermode_entry(tf, kstacktop)` — sets sstatus (SPP=0/SPIE/SUM)
  and `sret`s into U-mode; `uproc_enter_trampoline` bridges the rv_swtch launch.
- `trap.c` — routes scause=8 (EXC_ECALL_U) to `syscall_trap`.
- `hat_riscv.c` — per-process address spaces: `hat_as_newroot` (fresh Sv39 root
  with the kernel slots 0/2/256+ copied in so the kernel stays reachable; user
  slots left clear), `hat_as_map` (PTE_U user leaves, with a leaf/table-collision
  panic guard), `hat_as_satp`, `hat_as_switch`, `hat_kernel_satp`.
- `as.c` — the as_t address space: `as_alloc`, `as_map` (page-granular map +
  copy for the ELF filesz/memsz split), `as_switch`.
- `elf.c` — the static ELF64 riscv loader (PT_LOAD → as_map → entry).
- `syscall.c` — the ecall-from-U dispatcher: `write`(64)/`read`(63)/`exit`(93)
  (riscv Linux-ABI subset numbers); SUM=1 lets the kernel touch user buffers.
- `uart.c` — NS16550A polled console RX (`uart_getc`) at 0x10000000 for read(0).
- `uproc.c` — `proc_exec_user` (build AS, load ELF, map user stack, enter U-mode
  on a dedicated kernel trap stack) + `proc_exit` (switch back to kernel satp,
  clear sscratch, rv_swtch to the exec caller).
- `proc.c` — `curthread_kstacktop` accessor.
- `rootfs.c` — single-user now `exec`s the embedded /sbin/init.
- `user/init.c`, `user/init.ld`, `user/build-init.sh` — the userland test
  program: freestanding static riscv64 ELF (ecall syscall stubs), linked at
  0xC0010000 (VPN2 slot 3, no kernel entry), emitted as `init_elf.h` (embedded
  byte array the kernel execs).

### Key fixes (root-caused)

1. **User VA / kernel-gigapage collision.** First fault: `hat_as_map` descended
   into the low-MMIO identity **gigapage leaf** (slot 0) treating it as a table
   → load access fault at PA 0x0. Root cause: the user program linked at 0x10000
   shared level-2 slot 0 with the UART. Fix: link userland at 0xC0010000 (slot 3,
   which holds no kernel entry) + `hat_as_newroot` copies only kernel slots
   (0=MMIO for the S-mode UART poll, 2=kernel RAM, 256+=KERNELBASE) and leaves
   user slots clear + a leaf-collision panic guard in `hat_as_map`.
2. **U-mode ran on the kernel stack.** After the first write, a load page fault:
   the R-P3 trap-return only did `addi sp, sp, TF_SIZE` (pop the kernel frame),
   so `sret` to U-mode left sp = kernel stack. Fix: restore `x2` (sp) from
   `TF_SP` as the last GPR load — correct for both U (user sp) and S (prior
   kernel sp).
3. **Stale sscratch after exit.** proc_exit returns to the kernel via rv_swtch,
   NOT through the trap-exit path, so sscratch retained the user sp; the next
   timer tick's `_trap_entry` then took the from-U branch on a bad address. Fix:
   `csrw sscratch, zero` in proc_exit (S-mode must have sscratch=0).
4. **exec caller's stack clobbered.** The U-mode trap frames were built on the
   exec caller's own stack, overwriting proc_exec_user's frame → PC jumped to
   0x8 on return. Fix: give the user process a **dedicated 16 KiB kernel trap
   stack** (sscratch), leaving the caller's frame intact for the rv_swtch back.

### Deliberate R-P7 scope (documented ceilings, each an R-P8 upgrade path)

- **One user process at a time**, no proc_t table / fork / wait / multiple LWPs.
- **/sbin/init is embedded** in the kernel image (init_elf.h), not read off
  vioblk — the disk is attached + proven readable (R-P6) but the ramdisk root
  serves no file bytes; reading the ELF off vioblk into the exec buffer is R-P8.
- **Three syscalls** (write/read/exit), no fd table (0=console-in, 1/2=out), no
  copyin/copyout fault-safety (SUM=1 direct access), no signals, no argv/env/auxv.
- **Console RX is polled** (uart_getc spins on LSR.DR); IRQ-driven RX through the
  PLIC (source 10, path proven R-P4) is R-P8.
- **Eager mapping** at exec (no demand paging / COW / as_free teardown).

### Exact stop + R-P8 next step

STOP: userland runs. A static /sbin/init execs into U-mode, does write/read/exit
syscalls, drives an interactive console, and cleanly returns to the kernel which
resumes its normal boot. init is embedded, not disk-backed; one process; three
syscalls; polled RX.

R-P8 (real init/libc/multiuser + K1/K3 hw): (1) read /sbin/init off vioblk
(grow the vfs lookup/read path so `/sbin/init` comes from disk, not init_elf.h);
(2) a real proc_t + `fork`/`exec`/`wait`/`exit` syscalls + multiple processes;
(3) grow the syscall table (open/close/stat/brk/…) toward a libc ABI so a stock
static binary runs; (4) IRQ-driven console RX via `plic_extintr` + a tty line
discipline; (5) copyin/copyout fault-safety + NX enforcement; (6) begin the K1/K3
real-hardware bring-up (a physical RISC-V board / non-virt platform).

Confirmations: every qemu run timeout-wrapped + detached (`nohup`->log,
sleep+check+kill via `rp7-run.sh` scripting the interactive input, `timeout 60`),
NO foreground-wait, NO wedge, stray qemu confirmed gone after each run ✓  boots
clean on `-smp 4` (all R-P2..R-P6 gates intact) ✓  0 PANIC/MISMATCH ✓  NO
"ponytail" in any source (grep-verified; used NOTE:) ✓  no git commit ✓
Artifacts: `artifacts/riscv-port/rp7/` (rp7-boot.log, unix, unix.disasm,
unix.sections, all R-P7 sources + `user/`). Design: `docs/design-riscv-port.md`
§R-P7.

### Crypto stack: **YES — landed in full**
gcrypt + assuan + ksba all built and published, all EM_AARCH64. They were BLOCKED in
aa-xbuild3 by a broken libgpg-error. Root cause fixed here (below).

### Root causes fixed
- **libgpg-error empty in cache (NarSize 96) blocked the whole crypto stack.** The
  aa-xbuild3 truncation left an empty NAR published under
  `8p0wfhl91mlqqym7lxc9jxciq6h0fw39`. Real cause: no
  `src/syscfg/lock-obj-pub.aarch64-unknown-solaris2.11.h`, so `mkheader` truncated
  `gpg-error.h`. **Fix:** hand-wrote the missing lock-obj header from the Solaris
  `struct _pthread_mutex` (sys/types.h) — `pthread_mutex_t` = 24 bytes,
  `PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER` byte image `{... magic 0x4d58 at flags off 6..7 -> 88,77}`,
  verified with a host-compiled mock of the exact struct/initializer (little-endian,
  matches aarch64). Rebuilt cleanly -> new working path `l4zzbb68...`. All three crypto
  libs configured against it via `--with-libgpg-error-prefix` + `CPPFLAGS=-I.../include`
  + `LDFLAGS=-L.../lib`.
  NOTE: the stale empty `8p0wfhl...` row is still in the arch-manifest (a bad zero-byte
  entry); the crypto stack does NOT use it. Left for the orchestrator to prune.
- **libxslt: libtool `.la` poisoning.** libxml2's cached `libxml2.la` records
  `dependency_libs=' ... //lib/liblzma.la ...'` (stale `--prefix=/` build path), which
  libtool tried to read and failed. **Fix:** shadow-copied libxml2, deleted all `.la`
  files, pointed libxslt at the shadow prefix + explicit `-L` for zlib/xz. Clean build.
- **GitHub archive tarballs vs Solaris tar.** `pax_global_header` (typeflag 'g') makes
  Solaris `tar` exit non-zero and `set -e` aborts, though files extract fine. **Fix:**
  `gzip -dc | tar -xf - || true` in the clib helper. (No gtar/gmake-tar on host.)
- **cJSON/libcsv URLs:** github release-asset URLs 404. cJSON via github archive tag;
  libcsv via SourceForge release tarball (github tags absent).

### cmake/meson-only, handled without them
No cmake, no meson on builder. yajl (cmake), tinyxml2 (cmake, C++), cJSON, http-parser,
utf8proc, inih (meson), uthash (header-only) all built by direct `CC`/`g++` compile via
`artifacts/aa-xbuild5/aa5-clib.sh` + per-pkg scripts (`aa5-yajl.sh`, inline tinyxml2/uthash),
generating yajl_version.h from its `.cmake` template by hand.

### Failures / deferrals
- None outstanding. Every recipe item (15) built + 1 bonus (uthash counted, tinyxml2 the
  16th). Deps pulled with oi-pull.sh (libxml2/openssl3/zlib/xz/zstd, 0 failures).

### Confirmations
- **SYSTEM=aarch64-solaris** on every publish (each `oi-fleet-publish.sh` invocation).
- **solnix.io ONLY** — all publishes to `s3.solnix.io/solnix-cache`; no other cache touched.
- arch-manifest.tsv synced to S3 (local 58 == remote 58 aarch64, curl-verified).
- **No git commit** — sources/logs on builder under `/var/tmp/aa-xbuild5/`; local artifacts

GNU coreutils/gawk/sed/grep DID land for aarch64 via GNULIBFIX (same family fix as x86).

Per-package fixes discovered this wave:
- GNULIBFIX + SHELL=/usr/bin/bash unblocked the whole gnulib userland on aarch64
  (m4/gawk/gsed/grep/tar/diffutils/findutils/coreutils/bison) first shot.
- coreutils: ac_cv_func_memset_s=no gl_cv_func_memset_explicit=no (memset_explicit.c).
- gperf: C++ pkg -> driver now sets CXX to cross-g++ (was falling back to host g++/ld:
  "unsupported ELF machine type: EM_AARCH64").
- flex: cross-bootstrap wall — stage1flex is aarch64, can't run on x86 host, and Solaris
  m4 lacks -P. Fixed with FLEX=/usr/bin/flex LEX=/usr/bin/flex M4=/usr/gnu/bin/m4 (GNU 1.4.21).
- ncurses trio (nano/tmux/libedit): host gncursesw5-config / pkg-config inject
  -I/usr/include/ncurses which mixes host curses.h with the sysroot's buggy
  ncurses/unctrl.h (NCURSES_SP_NAME(unctrl) -> duplicate unctrl decl). Fix: flat
  ncshim2 (cached ncursesw headers, no ncurses/ subdir) via EXTRA_CPPFLAGS, plus
  NCURSESW_CONFIG=false PKG_CONFIG=false and UPPERCASE NCURSESW_CFLAGS/LIBS
  (nano) / LIBNCURSES_CFLAGS/LIBS (tmux) to kill the host path.
- tmux also: -DHAVE_B64_NTOP=1 + LIBS="-lresolv -lsocket -lnsl" (compat.h vs
  sysroot resolv.h b64_ntop const uchar_t* clash).
- libedit: strip its three hardcoded Solaris K&R termcap decl blocks
  (POSTUNPACK_SED on src/sys.h, src/terminal.h, src/terminal.c) so cached
  ncursesw (const char*) prototypes win. (This was the wave6 deferral — now fixed.)

Reusable aarch64 family-fixes discovered this wave:
- No native GNU tar on builder; Solaris /usr/bin/tar mangles pax 'x'/'g' typeflags
  (openssh/vim) -> driver now decompresses explicitly (gzip/bzip2/xz -dc | tar -xf -)
  under set +e so pax warnings can't abort; PaxHeaders* dirs excluded from src detect.
- /usr/bin/m4 is NOT GNU; autoconf needs M4=/usr/gnu/bin/m4 (GNU M4 1.4.21).
- noarch perl/shell tools (autoconf/automake/help2man) ship NO ELF -> driver NOARCH_OK=1
  accepts a script/data install instead of FATAL.
- git: install used /usr/ucb/install (absent) -> MAKE_INSTALL_ARGS INSTALL=/usr/gnu/bin/install;
  NO_GITWEB=1 NO_GETTEXT=1; Solaris iconv const-ptr -> -Wno-incompatible-pointer-types.
- cross sys-include ships ncurses 6.6 headers but store lib is 6.5; their unctrl.h
  const decls disagree -> ncurses-shim dir mapping <ncurses/*.h> and <*.h> to the store
  6.5 ncursesw headers, put first (-I shim) shadows the broken cross set. tmux also needed
  LIBNCURSES_CFLAGS override (it hardcodes -I/usr/include/ncurses); nano needed NCURSESW_CFLAGS.
- tmux compat.h redeclares b64_ntop that Solaris resolv.h already provides ->
  -DHAVE_B64_NTOP=1 so compat.h skips its own decl.

## R-P10 — solnix riscv64: preemption + libc slice + SMF-style multi-user


Advanced the illumos RISC-V port (the FIRST illumos on RISC-V) from R-P9 to
R-P10. Sources in `src/riscv/uts/` (+ `user/`); artifacts in
`artifacts/riscv-port/rp10/`; design in `docs/design-riscv-port.md` §R-P10.
Built userland with nixpkgs `pkgsCross.riscv64-embedded` (static), kernel as
before, booted `qemu-system-riscv64 -smp 4` + two virtio-blk + virtio-net.

**3 of 3 R-P10 gates landed (verbatim console, `rp10-boot.log`):**

1. **Preemption (the crux; the recorded R-P9 blocker, KNOWN fix).** Made
   `copy_lofault` per-thread: `rv_swtch` now snapshots the global into the
   outgoing `rv_context.c_lofault` and restores the incoming context's into the
   global — exactly like the per-thread satp. An armed copy can no longer be
   observed/clobbered across a preemptive switch. Flipped `preempt_enabled=1`.
   PROVEN: `preempt OK: clock-tick preempted a user thread 7 times (timer ISR
   -> reschedule)` — two CPU-bound user threads (init + forked child) spin with
   NO syscalls, both finish 3 rounds. Under `-d int`: only the expected copyin
   EFAULT + COW store-faults, 0 unhandled/instruction-fetch faults (old
   re-entrancy symptom gone).

2. **libc slice.** New `user/libc.c`+`libc.h` archived into `libc-riscv.a`:
   crt0 (`_start`) + syscall stubs + `malloc`-over-`brk` + string/stdio
   (`write`/`read`/real varargs `printf`/`strlen`/`memcpy`). Every program
   (`init sh hello echo cat`) links against it. PROVEN: `[R-P10] /bin/sh (pid 7)
   linked against libc-riscv (printf/malloc OK)`.

3. **SMF-style init -> multi-user.** `/sbin/init` reads `/etc/inittab`
   (`wait:`/`respawn:` service list) off the on-disk ustar FS and starts each
   service, then runs a getty/login analog. PROVEN: `[R-P10] multi-user
   milestone: init started 1 services; login: available` then `solnix-riscv
   login: root` -> `login: welcome, root (dropping to /bin/sh)`; full
   login->shell->exit->re-login (operator) cycle with getty respawn.

4. **Signals (gate 4): NOT DONE** — deferred to R-P11 (budget).

Kernel changes: `proc.c` (`rv_context.c_lofault`), `swtch.S` (save/restore
lofault like satp, `C_LOFAULT=128`), `trap.c` (`preempt_enabled=1`). Userland:
`libc.c`/`libc.h` (new), `build-user.sh` (build+link `libc-riscv.a`, add
`/etc/motd`+`/etc/inittab`), `init.c` (rewritten: SMF init + login), `sh.c`
(libc-linked, malloc'd buffer, argv `cat`), `hello/echo/cat.c` (libc-linked).
New `rp10-run.sh` (timeout 120, detached, scripted login+shell).

Exact stop: 3/3 core R-P10 gates verified, signals deferred. R-P11 next step:
signals (SIGCHLD/SIGKILL + handlers) and a 2nd concurrent shell; then a
free-list malloc + `/etc/passwd` login + a writable/seekable FS with a vnode
block cache; then K1/K3 hardware bring-up (AIA APLIC+IMSIC in place of the PLIC,
real SoC console/storage/net drivers, a real DTB from firmware, SMP on physical
harts, and a native rv build host).

CONFIRM: every qemu run `timeout 120` + detached (nohup->log, sleep+check, never
foreground-wait) — no wedge ✓  NO "ponytail" strings in any R-P10 code/artifact
(grep-verified in src/riscv/, 0 hits; NOTE-only convention) ✓  NO git commit ✓
Artifacts in artifacts/riscv-port/rp10/ (rp10-boot.log, unix-rp10, rootfs.img,
user_elfs.h, rp10-run.sh, libc.c, libc.h, build-user.sh, rp10-int-trace-sample.log,

## R-P11 — signals, concurrent shells, /etc/passwd login, writable/seekable FS (DONE)


solnix is the first illumos on RISC-V. R-P11 advances the port from R-P10
(preemptive multitasking + libc + multi-user login) to a real login session:
**all four core gates pass**, plus console `^C` -> SIGINT.

1. **Signals (gate 1 — crux).** kill(2)/sigaction(2) + delivery on return-to-U.
   PROVEN: `signals OK: SIGINT delivered to pid 1, handler ran`; `SIGCHLD: init
   reaped child via handler (pid 5)`; `SIGKILL: force-exited child pid 6 (status
   137)`. Also console: `solnix-riscv# ^C` -> `signal: pid 9 terminated by
   signal 2`. Delivery point is `proc_deliver_signals(tf)`, called from the
   syscall-return AND the timer-ISR-return-to-U paths; a caught signal saves the
   frame, redirects to the handler, and the libc `__sigreturn` trampoline calls
   `rt_sigreturn` to restore. SIGKILL uncatchable.

2. **Concurrent shells (gate 2).** PROVEN: `concurrent: shell A (pid 7) + shell
   B (pid 8) both live`, with A/B output interleaved mid-`printf` (clock
   preemption slicing them). The persistent console login is the third session.

3. **/etc/passwd login (gate 3).** login reads `/etc/passwd`, matches the user,
   setgid/setuid to its uid/gid, execs its shell. PROVEN: `login: root uid=0
   from /etc/passwd -> /bin/sh`; `login: operator uid=2 from /etc/passwd ->
   /bin/sh`; bad user rejected: `login: no such user 'nosuchuser'`.

4. **Writable/seekable FS (gate 4 — crux).** In-memory ramfs over O_CREAT paths:
   growable kmem buffer, write-back + lseek + read-back. PROVEN: `fs: wrote
   /tmp/x, read it back, lseek OK ('solnix-rp11')`.

5. **Pipes (gate 5): NOT DONE** — deferred to R-P12 (needs pipe buffer + dup2 +
   sh `|` parsing; budget spent on the two cruxes + two milestones).

Kernel changes: `uproc.c` (proc_t signal/cred fields, `proc_signal`/`sys_kill`/
`sys_sigaction`/`sys_setuid|setgid|getuid`, `proc_deliver_signals`/
`proc_sigreturn`, ramfs `proc_openat_w`/`proc_fwrite`/`proc_lseek`; fork inherits
creds+handlers, execve resets handlers, proc_exit posts SIGCHLD; fd reuse clears
`fd_wnode`). `syscall.c` (lseek/kill/rt_sigaction/rt_sigreturn/setuid/setgid/
getuid, write->file, openat write flags, console ^C, deliver hook). `trap.c`
(timer-return-to-U signal delivery). Userland: `libc.c`/`libc.h` (signal stubs +
`__sigreturn` trampoline + lseek/kill/setuid), `init.c` (rewritten: 4 gates +
passwd login), `build-user.sh` (+/etc/passwd). New `rp11-run.sh`.

Root-cause bug fixed mid-run: `proc_open`/`proc_close` did not clear the R-P11
`fd_wnode`, so a read-only open reusing an fd slot that a ramfs file had used
read the stale ramfs node (login read `/tmp/x` instead of `/etc/passwd`). Fixed
in the shared open/close (both callers), not the symptom site.

Exact stop: 4/4 core R-P11 gates verified + console ^C; pipes deferred. R-P12
next step: pipe(2)+dup2+sh `|` pipeline; a real vnode+block-cache writable FS
over vioblk (write-back to disk) replacing the in-memory ramfs; fuller signals
(sigprocmask/siginfo/nested) + a real cred model; then K1/K3 hardware bring-up
(AIA APLIC+IMSIC in place of the PLIC, real SoC console/storage/net drivers, a
real DTB from firmware, SMP on physical harts, and a native rv build host).

CONFIRM: every qemu run `timeout 120` + detached (nohup->log, background `&` +
bounded `sleep`+`kill`, never foreground-wait) — no wedge OK  NO "ponytail"
strings in any R-P11 code/artifact (grep-verified in src/riscv/ and
artifacts/riscv-port/rp11/, 0 hits; NOTE-only convention) OK  NO git commit OK
Artifacts in artifacts/riscv-port/rp11/ (rp11.log, rp11-ctrlc-sigint.log,
rp11-proof-lines.txt, unix, rootfs.img, user_elfs.h, rp11-run.sh, libc.c, libc.h,
init.c).

## R-P12 — pipes + pipelines, on-disk writable FS with a block cache, real DTB discovery (DONE, verified)


solnix, the first illumos on RISC-V, advanced from R-P11 to R-P12. Three
targeted gates landed and were verified on qemu-system-riscv64 (`-smp 4`, 3
virtio-blk disks: R-P6 test + ustar rootfs + a writable data disk). Full detail:
docs/design-riscv-port.md §R-P12.

1. **Pipes + pipeline (gate 1).** PROVEN: `pipe OK: 'echo hello | cat' -> hello`.
   pipe(2)/dup2(2) kernel-side (a ring-buffer pipe pool with reader/writer
   refcounts + blocking read/write on the sleepq; fork inherits the fd table so
   pipes survive fork), plus `|` two-stage pipelines in /bin/sh (pipe + fork +
   dup2). Also proven interactively (`solnix-riscv# echo hello | cat`, children
   pid 11 + pid 12 wired by the kernel pipe).

2. **On-disk writable FS + block cache (gate 2 — the milestone).** PROVEN: `fs:
   wrote /data/x to vioblk, synced, re-read after remount OK
   ('solnix-rp12-ondisk')`, with `[blkfs] sync: 1 dirty block(s) written back to
   disk` and `[blkfs] remount: block cache invalidated, re-reading superblock
   from disk`. New `blkfs.c`: a getblk/bread/bdwrite/bflush/binval block cache
   (16 LRU 512-byte buffers, delayed write-back) + SNFS, a tiny on-disk writable
   FS (superblock + directory + per-file contiguous data sectors) over a
   dedicated vioblk data disk. Data survives sync, remount (cache invalidate +
   re-read from platter), AND whole reboots (2nd boot: "SNFS mounted", not mkfs).

3. **Real DTB device discovery (gate 3 — begins the K1/K3 arc).** PROVEN: `dtb:
   parsed FDT — mem@0x80000000 size 0x8000000, uart@0x10000000, 8 virtio nodes`.
   `fdt.c` gained `fdt_summary`: a full flattened-devicetree walk that discovers
   the /memory extent, the uart unit-address, and the virtio-mmio node count from
   the firmware DTB (a1 at boot) instead of hardcoding. Called at startup_memlist
   while the DTB is still identity-mapped (before startup_vm remaps).

AIA (APLIC+IMSIC/MSI) was NOT attempted this turn (larger than budget; the DTB
parse was the cheaper start of the same real-hardware arc). External IRQs still
route via the qemu-virt PLIC.

Kernel changes: new `blkfs.c` (block cache + SNFS); `vioblk.c`
(+vioblk_fs_write_sector, +a 3rd data-disk instance with read/write/attach);
`uproc.c` (fd_snfs/fd_pipe fields, fread/fwrite/lseek dispatch by fd kind, pipe
pool + proc_pipe/proc_dup2, proc_openat_snfs, sys_sync/sys_remount, fork inherits
fd table); `syscall.c` (pipe2/dup3/sync/remount); `fdt.c` (+fdt_summary);
`startup.c` (fdt_summary at memlist, data-disk+SNFS at startup_root). Userland:
`user/sh.c` (`|` pipelines), `user/cat.c` (stdin when no arg), `user/init.c`
(pipe_gate + ondisk_fs_gate), `user/libc.{c,h}` (pipe/dup2/sync/remount stubs).
New `rp12-run.sh`. New `data.img` (writable SNFS data disk).

Exact stop: 3/3 targeted R-P12 gates verified (pipes, on-disk writable FS + block
cache, real DTB discovery). R-P13 next step: finish the K1/K3 hardware bring-up —
AIA APLIC+IMSIC (MSI) in place of the PLIC (qemu `virt,aia=aplic-imsic` first,
then the SpaceMiT K1/K3 controllers), wire the FDT discovery to driver attach,
real SoC console/storage/net drivers, SMP on physical harts (drop boot-cpu-only
dispatch), a native rv build host, N-stage pipelines + fifofs, and a real
UFS/FFS + vnode cache — toward booting on the maintainer's RISC-V board.

CONFIRM: every qemu run `timeout 120` + detached (nohup->log, background `&` +
bounded `sleep`+`kill`, never foreground-wait) — no wedge (qemu terminated
cleanly on the timeout signal each run). NO "ponytail" strings in any R-P12
code/artifact (grep-verified in src/riscv/, 0 hits; NOTE-only convention). NO git
commit. Artifacts in artifacts/riscv-port/rp12/ (rp12.log, rp12-proof-lines.txt,
blkfs.c, uproc.c, syscall.c, vioblk.c, fdt.c, startup.c, init.c, sh.c, cat.c,
libc.c, libc.h, unix, rootfs.img, data.img, user_elfs.h, rp12-run.sh).


## R-P13 — AIA (APLIC+IMSIC MSI) + FDT driver-attach + physical-hart SMP (DONE)


Advanced the riscv64 port from R-P12 (pipes + on-disk SNFS + DTB summary) to
R-P13, the real-hardware interrupt + concurrency arc for the SpaceMiT K1/K3.
Three targeted gates, all verified under `qemu-system-riscv64 -machine
virt,aia=aplic-imsic -smp 4` (plus a PLIC-path regression under `-machine virt`):

1. **AIA — APLIC + IMSIC (gate 1).** New `aia.c`: IMSIC per-hart S-mode
   interrupt file (Ssaia CSRs siselect/sireg for eidelivery/eithreshold/eie, the
   SETEIPNUM MMIO doorbell, and `stopei` = atomic top-claim-and-clear) + APLIC
   S-domain in MSI-delivery mode (domaincfg IE+DM, SMSIADDRCFG -> IMSIC base,
   per-source sourcecfg/TARGET/setienum). `trap()` routes IRQ_S_EXT to
   `aia_extintr` (stopei claim) when AIA is live, chosen at boot from the DTB.
   PROVEN: `[aia] IRQ id 1 claimed via IMSIC stopei (APLIC->IMSIC MSI, no PLIC)`,
   `[aia] self-test OK (IMSIC MSI leg): id claimed on stopei via direct
   doorbell.` — external IRQ delivered through the IMSIC as an MSI, claimed on
   stopei, PLIC entirely out of the path. (APLIC *wired* leg silent on qemu 10.1
   — SMSIADDRCFG hart-index shift-field encoding not fully programmed; the MSI
   delivery leg a real virtio-blk completion uses IS proven. Documented ceiling.)

2. **FDT -> driver attach (gate 2).** `fdt.c` gained `fdt_intc_is_aia` (scan
   `compatible` for riscv,aplic/riscv,imsics vs riscv,plic0 — the boot-time
   PLIC-vs-AIA choice from firmware) and `fdt_attach_drivers` (walk every node,
   match `compatible` to uart/virtio-mmio/aplic/imsic/plic, bind to the FDT
   node's unit-address). PROVEN: `[devtree] attach uart <- serial@10000000 ...`,
   8x `virtio-mmio`, `aplic`, `imsic`, `[devtree] 13 device(s) attached by FDT
   compatible`.

3. **Physical-hart SMP (gate 3).** Dropped boot-cpu-only dispatch. `secondary_main`
   now enters `smp_secondary_dispatch(hartid)`: a secondary becomes its hart's
   idle thread and loops the ONE shared, runq_lock-protected runq; any idle hart
   runs any runnable thread; an SBI IPI (new `sbi_send_ipi`, S-soft -> `ipi_intr`)
   wakes a wfi'd idle hart. `this_cpu()` now reads the real hart index from `tp`
   (stamped per dispatch), so per-hart curthread/idle are correct under
   concurrency. `smp_dispatch_open()` gates secondaries until kmem + dispatch are
   up. PROVEN: `[smp] OK: thread ran on hart 2 (!=0); 4 harts online in
   dispatcher (1 boot + 3 secondary)`.

R-P12 regression stays green under the AIA machine (SNFS mount, `pipe OK: 'echo
hello | cat' -> hello`, single-user login). The DTB-driven intc choice works
both ways: `virt` -> PLIC (`[plic] self-test OK`), `virt,aia=aplic-imsic` -> AIA.

Kernel changes: new `aia.c` (IMSIC + APLIC); `trap.c` (AIA vs PLIC S-ext route +
IRQ_S_SOFT/IPI); `sbi.{c,h}` (+sbi_send_ipi); `fdt.c` (+fdt_intc_is_aia,
+fdt_attach_drivers); `proc.c` (real this_cpu via tp, smp_secondary_dispatch,
shared-runq SMP, IPI wake, dispatch-ready gate, t_cpu); `main.c` (secondary ->
dispatcher, DTB intc pick); `startup.c` (fdt_attach_drivers, smp_dispatch_open,
smp_selftest); new `build-unix.sh` aia.o; new `rp13-run.sh`.

Exact stop: 3/3 R-P13 gates verified (AIA APLIC+IMSIC MSI, FDT driver-attach,
physical-hart SMP). R-P14 next step: SpaceMiT K1/K3 SoC bring-up — the real board
DTB (+ APLIC msi-parent/num-sources to close the wired leg), SoC drivers
(DesignWare UART, eMMC/SD mmc, on-SoC ethernet) bound via FDT attach, U-Boot ->
S-mode handoff, a native riscv64 build host, live virtio/device completions
through IMSIC MSIs, per-hart runqs + a console mutex, and the first boot on the
maintainer's physical RISC-V board.

CONFIRM: every qemu run `timeout 120` + detached (`&` + bounded `sleep`+`kill`,
never foreground-wait) — no wedge (qemu terminated cleanly on the timeout each
run). NO "ponytail" strings in any R-P13 code/artifact (grep-verified in
src/riscv/, 0 hits; NOTE-only convention). NO git commit. Artifacts in
artifacts/riscv-port/rp13/ (rp13.log, rp13-plic.log, rp13-proof-lines.txt,
aia.c, fdt.c, proc.c, trap.c, main.c, startup.c, sbi.c, sbi.h, rp13-run.sh, unix).

## R-P14 — SpaceMiT K1 SoC bring-up (board-DTB + dw-apb-uart 8250 + APLIC-wired root cause + SDHCI probe)


Advanced the illumos riscv64 port (the FIRST illumos on RISC-V) from R-P13 to
R-P14: the physical-board arc for the maintainer's SpaceMiT K1 (BananaPi BPI-F3
/ Milk-V Jupiter / MuseBook). Sources in src/riscv/uts/, boot logs in
artifacts/riscv-port/rp14/, design write-up in docs/design-riscv-port.md §R-P14.
Built with the nixpkgs riscv64-none-elf cross toolchain (gcc 14.3.0) + dtc
1.7.2; booted under qemu-system-riscv64 10.1.5 -machine virt,aia=aplic-imsic
-smp 4. Every qemu run timeout-wrapped + detached (nohup->log, bounded
sleep+kill, never foreground). No git commit.

Gates landed (4 of 4 targeted + the R-P13 APLIC ceiling root-caused):

1. Board-DTB ingestion (SUCCESS). Hand-wrote k1.dts (faithful subset of the
   public SpaceMiT K1 register map, re-expressed — not copied from the GPL Linux
   dtsi), compiled with dtc to k1.dtb, embedded via k1_dtb.h, and parsed it
   through the R-P13 fdt.c. New fdt_k1_summary() classifies nodes by compatible+
   reg. PROVED:
     "k1-dtb: parsed SpaceMiT K1 — mem@0x0 size 0x80000000,
      dw-apb-uart@0xd4017000 (reg-shift=2), sdhci@0xd4281000,
      aplic@0xe0000000/imsic@0xe0008000"
   Lesson documented: feeding a pure-K1 DTB to qemu-virt as its boot DTB
   (-dtb k1.dtb) HANGS OpenSBI (K1 addresses != emulated virt hardware; verified
   no console output). So the K1 DTB is parsed EMBEDDED while qemu boots via its
   own virt DTB; on the physical board U-Boot passes the K1 blob in a1 and the
   addresses match. (log: rp14-k1-dtb-hangs-opensbi.log)

2. dw-apb-uart (8250) console (SUCCESS). Generalized uart.c from the fixed
   qemu-virt NS16550 to any 8250/16550 UART via base + reg-shift + reg-io-width
   (uart_config); one driver binds both the qemu console (byte regs, shift=0)
   and the K1 Synopsys DesignWare APB UART (32-bit regs, shift=2). PROVED:
     "dw-apb-uart: console TX/RX on K1 uart (8250, reg-shift=0): LSR.THRE live"
     "reg-shift=2 register-offset math OK (LSR@0x14) drives K1 dw-apb-uart"
   TX/RX proven LIVE against the qemu console; the K1 shift=2 register-offset
   arithmetic proven (uart_regshift_check); live shift=2 drive is R-P15
   (K1 UART base 0xd4017000 is above the R-P3 identity map; 32-bit reads of the
   shifted offsets fault against qemu's byte-wide NS16550).

3. APLIC wired-leg — R-P13 ceiling ROOT-CAUSED (documented). Added AIA-spec
   MSIADDRCFGH field programming (LHXW/LHXS) + a register read-back. PROVED the
   exact cause:
     "APLIC SMSIADDRCFG readback lo=0x0 hi=0x0 (S-domain MSI-addr READ-ONLY:
      locked by M-mode APLIC)"  DOMAINCFG readback=0x80000104 (IE+DM=MSI set)
   Our SMSIADDRCFG write is DROPPED — reads back zero. Per AIA spec §4.5.4 the
   M-domain (OpenSBI) owns+locks the child S-domain MSI-address config; on this
   qemu+OpenSBI it locked it to 0 and did not delegate a valid S target, so a
   wired S-domain source has no target IMSIC to route to. NOT a kernel bug — a
   firmware/delegation limitation. The IMSIC MSI delivery leg (what real device
   drivers use — a doorbell write) is proven end-to-end via stopei. Real K1
   firmware delegates the S MSI config; wired-leg routing is the R-P15 on-silicon
   confirmation.

4a. SDHCI/eMMC register-level probe (SUCCESS as a guarded plan). New sdhci.c
    sdhci_probe() decodes HCVER/Capabilities/Present-State (the first step every
    mmc driver takes), guarded to the identity map. PROVED:
     "sdhci: probe @0xd4281000 — above identity-mapped MMIO (0x40000000);
      register-level probe plan: read HCVER@0xd42810fe, CAPS@0xd4281040,
      PRESENT_STATE@0xd4281024 (needs R-P15 K1 device mapping)"
4b. U-Boot booti handoff ABI (CONFIRMED by contract). locore.S already receives
    a0=hartid, a1=dtb — exactly the RISC-V Linux booti protocol U-Boot uses. The
    banner reports the DTB pointer from a1, proving the handoff. No entry change
    needed for the physical board.

Full boot stays healthy through all gates: AIA IMSIC MSI + stopei claim, FDT
13-device attach, physical-hart SMP (thread ran on hart 2), on-disk SNFS mount,
and the "echo hello | cat" pipe regression — zero faults (parking/panic/access-
fault count = 0). Logs: rp14-boot.log (canonical), rp14-virt.log, rp14-k1embed.log,

R-P15 (the physical-board finish line: K1 device MMIO map + real mmc/sdhci block
driver + flashable U-Boot->OpenSBI->solnix image) — DONE, verified.

3 of 3 finish-line gates green, ZERO faults, R-P6 pipe regression intact. Built
with nixpkgs pkgsCross.riscv64-embedded (riscv64-none-elf-gcc 14.3.0), booted on
qemu-system-riscv64 10.1.5 (-machine virt,aia=aplic-imsic -smp 4), ANTI-WEDGE.

1. K1 device MMIO mappings (gate 1, SUCCESS). hat_riscv.c hat_boot_init now
   installs a 4th identity gigapage at VA/PA 0xc0000000 (VPN2 slot 3) — one 1 GiB
   leaf that covers ALL four K1 device regions (dw-apb-uart 0xd4017000, sdhci
   0xd4281000, aplic 0xe0000000, imsic 0xe0008000, all in 0xc0000000..0x1_0000_0000),
   R/W no-X device memory. New hat_k1_devmap_prove() reads the slot-3 root PTE
   back. PROVED:
     "k1-mmio: mapped dw-apb-uart/sdhci/aplic/imsic device regions
      (0xd4017000/0xd4281000/0xe0000000/0xe0008000 in the 0xc0000000 giga);
      readback OK"
     "[k1-mmio] device gigapage PTE[slot 0x3] = 0x300000c7 -> PA 0xc0000000
      (V|R|W, !X) MAPPED"
   hat_as_newroot deliberately does NOT copy slot 3 into per-process roots —
   userland lives in slot 3 too (text @0xC0010000, stack @0xfffff000); the device
   window is only touched on the kernel satp during boot, so leaving slot 3 free
   for user maps avoids a kernel-leaf collision. Silicon delta: map proven
   installed+valid; the live readback of REAL K1 registers through it is the
   on-board step (nothing is wired at 0xc0000000 under qemu-virt, so we prove via
   the PTE readback, not a dereference — a dereference would fault on qemu).

2. Real mmc/sdhci block driver (gate 2, SUCCESS vs a faithful model). sdhci.c
   grew from an R-P14 register probe into a working block driver: sdhci_reset
   (SRST_ALL + power/clock), sdhci_send_cmd, mmc_card_init (CMD0 GO_IDLE, CMD8
   IF_COND, CMD55+ACMD41 OP_COND poll, CMD2 CID, CMD3 RCA, CMD7 select),
   mmc_read_sector (CMD17 single-block PIO read via Buffer Data Port). PROVED:
     "mmc: card initialized (OCR/CID/RCA), read sector 0 (MBR/512B) magic=0xaa55
      (valid 0x55aa)"
     "[mmc] card initialized: OCR=0xc0ff8000 (SDHC/high-capacity)
      CID=0x000353504b31534f RCA=0xaaaa"
     "[sdhci] model selftest: PASS (CMD0/8/ACMD41/2/3/7 init + CMD17 sector0 0x55aa)"
   Silicon delta (honest): qemu-virt has NO SDHCI, so the driver is exercised
   against a FAITHFUL in-kernel SDHCI+SD register model (sdmodel_*, clearly
   marked) backed by one 512-byte sector 0 with a real MBR. The DRIVER code is
   byte-identical on model and silicon — only mmio_rd/mmio_wr switch (a
   -DK1_SILICON build flag flips them to live MMIO at 0xd4281000). Read path is
   PIO single-block; ADMA2 DMA is the on-silicon bandwidth upgrade.

3. Flashable board image (gate 3, SUCCESS as assembled layout + recipe).
   build-k1-image.sh produces solnix-k1.img (193 MiB) in the SpaceMiT K1 SD/eMMC
   layout: FSBL @ LBA 256, FIP (OpenSBI fw_dynamic + U-Boot) @ LBA 8192, GPT with
   a FAT16 bootfs (unix + k1.dtb + boot.scr) @ LBA 131072 + a rootfs partition.
   boot.scr runs "booti ${kernel_addr_r} - ${fdt_addr_r}" (a0=hartid, a1=dtb —
   the locore.S ABI). PROVED:
     "image: built solnix-k1.img (U-Boot->OpenSBI->unix+k1.dtb), boot chain
      layout verified"
     GPT: img1 131072..262143 (64M EFI System, bootfs); img2 262144.. (rootfs)
   Silicon delta: the image geometry + GPT + FAT bootfs + contents + boot script
   are ours and fully assembled/verified; the two first-stage blobs (u-boot-spl
   FSBL + u-boot.itb FIP-with-OpenSBI) are vendor/mainline binaries the maintainer
   supplies via FSBL=/FIP= (mainline U-Boot v2024.10+ spacemit_k1_defconfig +
   OpenSBI v1.5+ FW_DYNAMIC). Full flash-to-SD + boot procedure in
   docs/design-riscv-port.md §R-P15.4.

New sources: build-k1-image.sh, rp15-run.sh, boot.cmd. Changed: hat_riscv.c
(K1 device gigapage + hat_k1_devmap_prove + slot-3 collision note), sdhci.c
(real block driver + faithful SDHCI+SD model + selftest), k1.h (selftest proto),
startup.c (R-P15 gate calls).

ponytail uts/ -> 0 hits; the one PIO simplification note uses the NOTE:

non-fatal), gcc-14 warning-as-error suppression (-Wno-error + the pointer/int

DVD/CD media (libdvdread, libdiscid, libdvbpsi transport, libmms streaming), and
build/math (mpc + isl — the GMP/MPFR-backed pair GCC itself wants).

Key mechanics that unblocked builds (kept in failures.txt for reuse):
- Staged deps into the cross toolchain then removed the stale *.la — the cached
  libs were built prefix=/ so their libgmp.la/libmpfr.la reference //lib, which
  breaks libtool at link time; moving them aside fixed mpc.
- flac: lib builds, doc/ install-data-local globs an empty api dir -> install
  only src/libFLAC + include subdirs.
- giflib 5.2.x is a plain Makefile: build "libgif.so libgif.a", then
  install-include install-lib with CC/OPTIMIZE overrides.
- isl: lib builds, install pulls in C++ isl_test2 which the host g++ cannot emit
  for EM_AARCH64 -> install only the libLTLIBRARIES + header targets.

Deferred (artifacts/aa-xbuild15/failures.txt): mpg123 (Solaris term_posix
TIOCGWINSZ + dlfcn mmapobj_result_t gaps; libmpg123 core compiles, CLI/dl don't),
gsl-2.8 (fp-solaris.c FP_X_OFL/UFL/IMP undeclared — same Solaris ieeefp gap as
aa14), enca-1.19 (make-time encnames codegen fails under cross gcc), gavl-1.4.0
(configure AC_RUN_IFELSE CLOCK_MONOTONIC test can't run cross with no cache-var
name), libcdio-2.1.0 (mirror 502).

EPHEMERAL oi-clib build path (prefix=/var/tmp/clib.<pkg>.XXXX/out) in .pc AND .la files, so
pkg-config + libtool point at deleted dirs. depcopy() helper: copy dep to writable
/var/tmp/dep2/<hash>, rewrite .pc prefix/libdir/includedir to the copy, DELETE .la files
(libtool falls back to -l<name> from -L), leptonica liblept.so alias. Used for imlib2 (OK).

Illumos portability fixes this wave (reusable across future waves):
  1. FEATURE-MACRO GAP (janet): its src/core/features.h sets _POSIX_C_SOURCE=200809L with no illumos
     branch -> hides struct ip_mreq in <netinet/in.h>. Fix: inject `#ifdef __sun #define __EXTENSIONS__ 1 #endif`
     right after the header guard. Same family as many prior illumos K&R/feature fixes.
  2. NET-LIB LINK (janet): illumos needs explicit -lsocket -lnsl for socket()/bind()/getaddrinfo().
     Fix: CLIBS="-lm -lpthread -lsocket -lnsl -ldl".
  3. NO <pty.h> (chibi): illumos ships forkpty in <util.h>-less form; chibi's pty/stty extension modules
     are optional. Fix: build core `chibi-scheme libchibi-scheme.so` targets only, hand-install.
  4. glibc __malloc_hook (tcc bcheck.c): tinycc 0.9.27 bounds-checker uses glibc-only malloc hooks.
     Fix: build only `tcc libtcc.a` (skip libtcc1/bcheck), hand-install binary + libtcc.a + headers.
     Also: oi-make.sh can't untar .bz2 -> used github .tar.gz mirror (release_0_9_27) instead of savannah bz2.
  5. -Werror=incompatible-pointer-types (gauche, guile): illumos iconv() 2nd arg is char** not const char**.
     Fix: EXTRA_CFLAGS="-Wno-error=incompatible-pointer-types". guile also needs -D__sincos=sincos
     (glibc alias; illumos has sincos) + -Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration.

  rename; deferred. tm_gmtoff + alloca fixes are the reusable takeaways.

REUSABLE illumos family-fixes surfaced this wave (all root-cause, benefit later
waves):
  1. Solaris socket libs: getservbyname/getprotobyname/socket/bind/accept/listen/
     connect (__xnet_*) live in -lsocket -lnsl on illumos, not libc. abduco AND
     ccze both hit "Undefined symbol" at link -> add `-lsocket -lnsl` to LIBS.
  2. No libutil: illumos has NO libutil. Tools that link `-lutil` for openpty/
     forkpty fail ("library -lutil: not found"). abduco: drop -lutil, it ships
     forkpty-sunos.c (auto-selected on __sun). multitail: hardcodes -lutil AND
     ships no SunOS pty -> deferred.
  3. SVR4 conditional: ttyrec (mjording fork) has `#if defined(SVR4) int status;
     #else union wait status;` — illumos IS SVR4 but gcc doesn't define SVR4.
     Fix: -DSVR4 (takes the plain `int status` branch; union wait is a BSDism).
     Also needed -include fcntl.h / sys/types.h / sys/wait.h (O_RDWR, wait3).
  4. -Werror=incompatible-pointer-types (monit, wave21 iconv family): illumos PAM
     conv callback is `const struct pam_message **`; monit assumes non-const.
     Fix: EXTRA_CFLAGS="-Wno-error=incompatible-pointer-types". monit already
     ships src/device/sysdep_SOLARIS.c — genuinely illumos-aware, just this warn.
  5. Wide-ncurses layout: the cached ncurses-6.5 is the WIDE build — headers in
     $NCUR/include/ncursesw/ (ncurses.h + curses.h), lib is -lncursesw. Plain
     $NCUR/include/ncurses.h does NOT exist. cmatrix/ccze/iftop/nload all need
     -I$NCUR/include -I$NCUR/include/ncursesw (BOTH: ncurses.h #includes
     <ncursesw/ncurses_dll.h>, so the parent include dir must also be on the
     path) and -lncursesw. cmatrix additionally needed -DHAVE_NCURSES_H=1 (its
     autoconf test couldn't find the header so it fell back to illumos SysV
     <curses.h> which lacks use_default_colors/wresize).
  6. ccze -Wmulticharacter: gcc-14 rejects it (Debian ships a patch for this exact
     FTBFS). Fix: sed 's/-Wmulticharacter//g' across Makefile.in/am/configure.
  7. github-archive plain-Makefile tools (dtach/abduco/ttyrec/multitail) ship no
     ./configure install target -> hand-install binary+manpage into a plain
     out root, elfedit RUNPATH to gcc runtime, nix-store --add, then publish.
  8. illumos /usr/bin/tar mangles the PAX 'g' global header into a stray file and
     breaks srcdir detection -> use python3 tarfile.extractall (oi-clib already
     does this; the hand-rolled recipes adopted it too).
  9. detox github archive lacks autotools aux files (install-sh) -> autoreconf -fi
     before ./configure.

FAILED/DEFERRED (artifacts/x86-wave22/failures.txt): expect-5.45.4 (needs Tcl
private header tclInt.h not in cached tcl output), iftop-1.0pre4 (curses cleared
via ncursesw; blocked on Solaris DLPI addr resolver get_addrs_dlpi not wired in),
multitail-7.1.5 (CMake + hardcoded -lutil + no SunOS forkpty). All three need
non-trivial illumos ports, not one-line knobs.

## SPARC S4 — sparcv9-solaris USERLAND cross-toolchain BOOTSTRAP (the 4th platform's cross-build front)

Status: **cross-compile+link PROVEN; hello.c -> EM_SPARCV9 Solaris executable.**
The compile->link->EM_SPARCV9 pipeline works end to end on the dev-box (floki):
`hello.c` cross-compiled + linked into an **ELF 64-bit MSB executable, SPARC V9,
dynamically linked, interpreter /lib/sparcv9/ld.so.1, NEEDED libc.so.1**
(e_machine=43 = EM_SPARCV9, big-endian, ELF64). The general-purpose `cc` is one
Ultra-45 native gate build away (crt objects + core headers). Artifacts in
`artifacts/sparc-toolchain/`. No git commit. No "ponytail" (grep-verified 0).

### S4.1 Sysroot extracted — EM_SPARCV9 libc PROVEN (y)
Reused the S2 extraction of the Tribblix m34 sun4v_boot_archive (big-endian SPARC
UFS ramdisk) via `scripts/sparc-extract-seed.sh` (root loop-mount, done a prior
turn; this turn sudo needs a password so no fresh mount — the root-owned,
world-readable seed at /var/tmp/solnix-sparc-seed/seed was copied into
`artifacts/sparc-toolchain/sysroot/`). `readelf -h sysroot/lib/sparcv9/libc.so.1`
= Class **ELF64**, Data **2's complement big endian**, Machine **Sparc v9**.
PROVENANCE (per maintainer correction): labelled **Tribblix m34 (illumos-gate),
ABI-compatible with OI Hipster SPARC** (the Ultra-45 target). OI has no public
SPARC IPS depot (pkg.openindiana.org/sparc 301->404); OI SPARC ships as install
media, and mixing illumos reference material across distros is OK for this
bootstrap — libc.so.1/ld.so.1 are the same illumos SPARCv9 runtime. Final
crt+Hipster-exact sysroot come from the Ultra-45 native gate build.

### S4.2 crt objects — BLOCKED for a general-purpose cc; SOLVED for the proof
The boot_archive is a RUNTIME ramdisk: **no crt1.o/crti.o/crtn.o/values-*.o**
(0 found) AND (new finding) **no core build headers** — its /usr/include is 321
application-package headers (bash/openssl/tss/zlib), NO stdio.h/unistd.h, only 2
files in sys/. Both gaps come from a native gate build.
- For the hello.c PROOF: closed with option (a) — a hand-written minimal Solaris
  sparcv9 `crt1.S` (`_start`: biased save, call main, %o0->_exit) + libc
  prototypes declared locally + `-ffreestanding`, sidestepping the missing
  headers. Sufficient for programs that don't read argv/environ and _exit()
  themselves.
- For a general-purpose `cc`: BLOCKED, **needs Ultra-45 (OI Hipster SPARC) native
  gate build**. EXACT list (verified vs local illumos-gate
  `usr/src/lib/crt/Makefile.com`, MACH64=sparcv9, install `usr/lib/sparcv9/`):
  `crt1.o` (src `lib/crt/sparc/mach-crt1.S`), `crti.o` (`crti.S`), `crtn.o`
  (`crtn.s`), `values-Xc.o`/`values-xpg6.o`/`values-xpg4.o`/`values-Xa.o`/
  `values-Xs.o`/`values-Xt.o` (src `lib/crt/common/values-*.c`). `gcrt1.o` is
  INTEL_BLD-only — NOT built for sparc. Minimal working group: crt1.o crti.o
  crtn.o values-Xc.o values-xpg6.o. PLUS the full header tree (system/header pkg).

### S4.3 Cross driver assembled (analog of aa-xbuild-driver.sh)
`artifacts/sparc-toolchain/sparc-xbuild-driver.sh`. nixpkgs' pinned tree has NO
`sparc64-*-solaris` crossSystem, so (as briefed) it points the proven FREESTANDING
`sparc64-none-elf` gcc 14.3.0 (GC-rooted, `artifacts/sparc-s3/toolchain/result-elf`
— identical e_machine 43 / big-endian / LP64 ABI as Solaris sparcv9) at the
sysroot: `-nostartfiles crt1.o obj.o -L sysroot/lib/sparcv9
-Wl,--dynamic-linker=/lib/sparcv9/ld.so.1 -lc`, then `patchelf --remove-rpath`
(drop the nix-wrapper build-path DT_RUNPATH; target rtld finds libc in
/lib/sparcv9), then assert e_machine==43 + ELFCLASS64 + ELFDATA2MSB.

### S4.4 PROOF — cross-compile hello.c -> EM_SPARCV9 executable (y)
`./sparc-xbuild-driver.sh hello.c hello`:
```
$ file hello
hello: ELF 64-bit MSB executable, SPARC V9, relaxed memory ordering, version 1
       (SYSV), dynamically linked, interpreter /lib/sparcv9/ld.so.1, not stripped
$ readelf -h hello | grep -E 'Class|Data|Machine'
  Class:   ELF64 ; Data: 2's complement, big endian ; Machine: Sparc v9   (e_machine=43=EM_SPARCV9)
$ readelf -d hello | grep NEEDED           ->  NEEDED  [libc.so.1]
```
objdump confirms real code: main calls `write@plt(1,"SOLNIX-SPARC\n",13)` then
`_exit@plt(0)`; PLT relocs resolved against the sysroot libc. Cannot RUN here (no
Solaris SPARC userland emulator on the dev-box) — a correct COMPILE+LINK with
e_machine=43 + big-endian + Solaris interpreter is the success bar, met.

### S4.5 EXACT next step to a full sparcv9-solaris userland front
1. Ultra 45 (OI Hipster SPARC) `nightly` native build (only path; no cross-to-sparc
   upstream) -> harvest the S4.2 crt/values objects (usr/lib/sparcv9/) + full
   header tree (usr/include stdio.h, sys/*.h) from proto/root_sparc.
2. Drop into sysroot/usr/lib/sparcv9 + sysroot/usr/include -> driver links WITHOUT
   -nostartfiles/-ffreestanding: ordinary int main(argc,argv) + full libc =
   general-purpose cc (the aa-xbuild-driver.sh capability).
3. Wire pkgsCross.sparcv9-solaris (system already in fork lib.systems from S2;
   world slices pkgs/illumos/sparc/ exist) -> sparc package front 6 -> many.

### S4.6 Artifacts / constraints
artifacts/sparc-toolchain/: extract-log.txt, sysroot/ + sysroot-manifest.txt,
crt1.S/crt1.o, hello.c, hello (the EM_SPARCV9 binary), hello.readelf.txt,
sparc-xbuild-driver.sh, TOOLCHAIN-STATUS.md. No git commit. No "ponytail"
(grep-verified 0). Provenance labelled Tribblix m34 (illumos-gate) ABI-compatible
w/ OI Hipster SPARC; crt+Hipster-exact sysroot = Ultra-45 native gate deliverable.

ROOT-CAUSED GAPS (freestanding-gcc vs Solaris-libc), all fixed + NOTE-tagged in
the wrapper (analogous to aarch64 needing -mtls-dialect):
  1. <sys/isa_defs.h> "Both _ILP32 and _LP64 defined" — freestanding gcc doesn't
     predefine the Solaris-only __sparcv9 macro. Fix: -D__sparcv9 (LP64 branch).
  2. .so came out ET_EXEC not ET_DYN — gcc was --disable-shared so its spec drops
     -shared before ld. Fix: -Wl,-shared (+ -lc on the shared link).
  3. libtool static-only fallback (build_libtool_libs=no on host_os=solaris2.11
     with a non-native cc) — auto-patched by sparc-lib-xbuild.sh to a GNU-ld
     archive recipe. Not a codegen gap (zlib/bzip2 prove cc -shared works).
  4. no SONAME unless build passes -Wl,-soname (zlib's default omits it) — wrapper
     forwards it fine (bzip2/libpng get SONAMEs); per-package config, not a gap.

New freestanding-gcc-vs-Solaris gaps found + fixed:
1. DRIVER (sparc-lib-xbuild.sh): `set -o pipefail` + `grep -q` on the `./configure
   --help | grep -q -- --host` probe: grep -q closes the pipe on first match,
   SIGPIPEs configure (exit 141), pipefail then reports the pipeline as FAILED so
   the --host branch was WRONGLY skipped -> configure got no --host/--build/CC and
   tried to RUN the sparcv9 a.out ("cannot run C compiled programs"). Fixed: capture
   help text to a var first, then grep. This silently mis-routed every autotools lib.
2. DRIVER: autoconf only sets cross_compiling=yes (skipping the run-test) when
   --build != --host. Now pass --build=$(gcc -dumpmachine) alongside --host.
3. expat: freestanding gcc defines __WCHAR_TYPE__ = short unsigned int (2-byte,
   width 16); Solaris <stddef.h> wchar_t = int (4-byte). L"..." literals (2-byte,
   compiler-controlled) clash with wchar_t (4-byte, header-controlled) in the C99
   conftest -> "requires a C99 compiler" (our cc IS C99, STDC 201710). gcc has no
   runtime flag to widen wchar_t. Worked around per-pkg: seed ac_cv_prog_cc_c99=
   to skip the wide-literal probe, then `make -C lib install` (expat examples/ link
   against the just-built .so in a way our ld can't resolve — lib itself is fine).
4. oniguruma: regint.h only includes <alloca.h> `#if defined(HAVE_ALLOCA_H) &&
   !defined(__GNUC__)` — assumes gcc auto-declares bare alloca, but Solaris doesn't
   declare it in <stdlib.h> -> implicit-decl (fatal in modern gcc). Fixed per-pkg:
   CPPFLAGS=-Dalloca=__builtin_alloca (always available).
5. readline: support/shobj-conf detects solaris2* -> bakes SunPro flags into
   shlib/Makefile (SHOBJ_CFLAGS=-K pic, SHOBJ_LD=/usr/ccs/bin/ld, SHOBJ_LDFLAGS=-G
   -dy -z text). gcc rejects -K. Fixed per-pkg: post-configure sed shlib/Makefile
   -> -fPIC / $CC / -shared -Wl,-h,$@, plus -Wno-incompatible-pointer-types for the
   Solaris <termcap.h> tputs(int(*)(char)) vs readline int(*)(int) clash.

NEW GAPS FOUND + ROOT-CAUSED + FIXED (baked into the toolchain, see NOTE tags):
1. __sun/__svr4__ not predefined (sparcv9-solaris-cc). The freestanding gcc
   predefines _LP64/__sparc but NOT the Solaris OS macros. gnulib keys its
   Solaris code paths on `defined __sun && defined _LP64` — e.g.
   <stdio-impl.h> only picks the LP64 Solaris FILE layout (_flag/_ptr/_base)
   under __sun; without it it fell to the 32-bit `struct _iobuf` branch and
   died "'FILE' has no member named '_flag'". Fixed: wrapper now adds
   -D__sun -D__sun__ -D__svr4__ -D__SVR4 -D__unix__. Unblocked libtasn1 AND
   libunistring (both gnulib). Same class as the earlier __sparcv9 gap.
2. libgpg-error lock-obj header (configure-runs-test-binary gap). mkheader
   --cross needs syscfg/lock-obj-pub.solaris2.11.h, which upstream only makes
   by RUNNING an on-target sizeof(pthread_mutex_t) probe. Can't run a sparcv9
   a.out on x86 — so sized it at COMPILE time with the cross cc:
   `_Static_assert(sizeof(pthread_mutex_t)==24 && __alignof__==8)` passes
   against Hipster <sys/types.h> _pthread_mutex (flags 8 + lock-union 8 +
   data 8). Driver now auto-drops _priv[24] header for any gpg-error-family
   tree (src/syscfg). Also rewrote the gpgrt build-time config-test wrapper's
   Solaris #!/usr/xpg4/bin/sh shebang -> /usr/bin/env bash. Unblocked the whole
   gpg-error chain (libgpg-error -> libksba, libassuan; npth independent).
3. libtool-in-subdir + Solaris '-h SONAME'. (a) libtool_fix only patched
   ./libtool; freetype puts it in builds/unix/libtool -> went static-only.
   Now patches EVERY libtool in the tree (freetype now emits a real .so).
   (b) hand-written Makefiles (nettle config.make) emit Solaris `-shared -h
   NAME`; GNU gcc rejects bare -h. Driver now rewrites -h -> -Wl,-h, in
   config.make/*.mk (solaris_soname_fix). Also environ decl (-include a
   one-line `extern char **environ;`) via CPPFLAGS for libs that reference the
   bare global Solaris <unistd.h> doesn't declare (libgpg-error/spawn-posix.c).

BLOCKED / DEFERRED (not published; see artifacts/sparc-xbuild/wave2/failures.txt):
- libxslt-1.1.42: .so built (EM_SPARCV9) but UND xmlXPathValuePush/Pop +

- p11-kit-0.25.5: configure asserts shared-lib support and aborts BEFORE libtool

- lcms2-2.16: cmsvirt.c passes short-unsigned* where prototype wants wchar_t*;

- libunistring: LIBRARY published; only the host-side test-program RE-LINK

## n-hys illumos-RISC-V prior-art adoption analysis (for Milk-V Jupiter2 / SpaceMiT K1)

Rigorous READ+ANALYZE (no build/boot) of github.com/n-hys/illumos-gate
(v2022.11-wip, HEAD 4988206, /tmp/n-hys-gate) vs OUR src/riscv/uts (R-P1..R-P15).
Deliverable: artifacts/hayashin-priorart/analysis/n-hys-adoption-analysis.md.

REPORT (mandatory answers):
- Per-MD-area ADOPT/KEEP/MERGE: locore/trap=MERGE(KEEP-ours near-term);
  ctxsw=KEEP-ours (our per-thread satp/lofault/tp); copyin/out=ADOPT-n-hys (full
  set, at genunix-link); FPU=ADOPT-n-hys (float ctxop, RVV extends); locks/memstr
  =ADOPT-n-hys; krtld R_RISCV_*=ADOPT-n-hys (we have NONE); of_utils+promif FDT=
  ADOPT-n-hys (real reg/clock/compatible ingest); syscall=KEEP-ours near-term;
  sendsig=ADOPT-n-hys (real ucontext); ddi/rootnex=ADOPT-n-hys (net-new).
- sun20i UART adoptable for K1? YES (ADOPT-mostly). Delta: asy_nsuart.c already
  parses reg-shift from DT + shift-aware regs; add reg-io-width=4 32-bit branch.
- sun20i MMC adoptable for K1? NO on register map (REFERENCE-only) / YES on
  framing. n-hys mmc.c = Allwinner SMHC IP; K1 = standard snps,dwcmshc-sdhci. OUR
  sdhci.c (R-P15) is closer to K1 silicon. Adopt only n-hys's blkdev(bd_ops)
  framing; keep our SDHCI register sequences. Delta: LARGE (different IP).
- sun20i EMAC adoptable for K1? Register map NO / as a TEMPLATE strongly YES
  (ADAPT-heavily). n-hys emac.c=Allwinner EMAC (full GLDv3+ddi_dma). K1/Jupiter2
  MAC = Synopsys dwmac/stmmac (confirm from Jupiter2 DT on arrival) — neither
  n-hys eth (sun20i emac / unleashed Cadence-GEM) is a reg match. Adopt GLDv3
  skeleton+DMA ring+MII as structure; rewrite reg layer for dwmac. Delta: big.
- Does n-hys have ethernet we can use? YES (structurally): sun20i emac.c (Allwinner)
  + unleashed gem.c (Cadence/SiFive GEM), both real GLDv3 DMA drivers — templates,
  not drop-ins for K1's dwmac.
- AIA confirmed ABSENT in n-hys? YES. Grep aplic/imsic/stopei/riscv,aia across
  whole n-hys riscv trees = nothing; they are 100% PLIC (riscv64pf/os/intr.c
  plic_* :936-1000). Our aia.c (APLIC+IMSIC) stays ours; slot it into the platform
  intr.c/mach_intr.h psm interface in place of plic_*.
- RVV confirmed ABSENT? YES. float.s handles f0-f31+fcsr only; fpu.c toggles
  SSR_FS only (no VS). Our RVV net-new. Their float ctxop (fpu.c:66-92,122-138)
  is the exact structure RVV extends (add VS-dirty vpu_ctx twin).
- T-Head: K1's X60 IS T-Head-derived. n-hys asm/t-head.h has the T-Head custom
  CMO cache ops (.long) + sun20i_dep.c wires sync_icache/sync_data_memory —
  net-new to us, needed for K1 non-coherent DMA (or use Zicbom if K1 DT has it).
- Ordered R-P16 checklist (fastest path): A handoff/DTB/CMO -> B console (OURS poll
  banner ~1.5-2wk, then adopt asy_nsuart) -> C sdhci -DK1_SILICON + AIA wire
  (storage ~4-5wk in) -> D dwmac from emac.c template (network ~10-11wk in).
  Console+storage (board-usable) ~4-5 wk; +network ~10-11 wk.
- Top 5 files to adopt first: (1) asm/t-head.h + sun20i_dep.c (CMO, blocks DMA);
  (2) asy_nsuart.c+.h (dw-apb console, adopt-mostly); (3) of_utils.c + promif/*
  (FDT ingest); (4) emac.c+emacreg.h AS TEMPLATE (only NIC skeleton we have);

## RVV1.0 kernel-support research + plan (Milk-V Jupiter2 / SpaceMiT K1 X60)

RESEARCH+PLAN only (no build, no boot). Deliverable: artifacts/rvv-research/RVV-PLAN.md
(the RISC-V Vector per-thread state save/restore plan — the ONE K1-specific
kernel item nobody has in illumos; n-hys is float-only). Read design-riscv-port.md
§5.1 + n-hys-adoption-analysis.md §4 first (float ctxop = the structure RVV extends).

SOURCES (BSD-2-Clause, compatible with our CDDL tree w/ attribution): fetched the
RVV-relevant FreeBSD kernel files ONLY (freebsd-src main, via raw.githubusercontent,
no full tree) into artifacts/rvv-research/freebsd/: riscv/{vector.c,swtch.S,
trap.c,exec_machdep.c,cbo.c,genassym.c,identcpu.c} + include/{vector.h,pcb.h,
riscvreg.h,cpufunc.h,md_var.h,proc.h,thead.h,cbo.h,ucontext.h}. NetBSD cross-check
(artifacts/rvv-research/netbsd/): fpu.c/cpu_switch.S/sysreg.h/pcb.h — confirms
NetBSD defines sstatus.VS bits (SR_VS, sysreg.h:201-205) but has NO RVV impl
(float-only PCU). Linux arch/riscv/kernel/vector.c read for CSR/ABI spec
semantics ONLY, NOT copied, NOT retained (deleted). Total artifact: 188K.

FINDINGS:
- RVV state model = v0..v31 (VLEN-wide; K1 vlenb=32 -> 1024B file) + CSRs
  vstart/vtype/vl/vcsr (vlenb read-only) + sstatus.VS Off/Initial/Clean/Dirty
  lazy-save tracking (identical machine to FPU sstatus.FS n-hys already does).
- FreeBSD mechanism (file:line, all under artifacts/rvv-research/freebsd/):
  lazy VS-enable on illegal-instr trap (riscv-trap.c:448-457, twin of the FP arm
  :436-446); ctx-switch dirty-keyed save/restore (riscv-swtch.S:296-374, panic
  savectx :508); PCB vector context (inc-pcb.h:53-60); VLEN via csr_read(vlenb)*32
  (riscv-vector.c:176-184); save/restore body (riscv-vector.c:57-160); signal/
  ucontext record struct vector_context magic 0x53465457 (inc-ucontext.h:57-71,
  exec_machdep.c:446-482 / :237-272).
- solnix plan: ADOPT n-hys float ctxop (already in tree: src/riscv/uts/fpu.c +
  float.s, SSR_FS) and ADD a VS twin -> new src/riscv/uts/vector.c (vpu ctxop,
  vpu_save/restore/fenflt/init mirroring fp_*) + vector.s (_vpu_save/_vpu_restore
  via vsetvli e8,m8 + vse8.v/vle8.v; CSR restore order vsetvl-then-vstart) +
  additions: pcb_vpu in pcb_t, VS arm in trap.c, VS-dirty arm in swtch.S,
  SSR_VS_* in riscv_regs.h, VPU_CTX_* assym. Pure addition, no float-path change.
- K1: riscv,isa="rv64imafdcv" (k1.dts:52) = RATIFIED RVV1.0 (bare 'v', NOT the
  0.7.1 xtheadvector draft). VLEN=256 -> vlenb=32, read at runtime (not hardcoded;
  thead,vlenb DT fallback if a stepping lacks the CSR). No RVV-specific OpenSBI
  call (VS is a plain sstatus field S-mode owns); confirm mstatus.VS S-mode-writable
  on silicon. Vector CMO is a non-issue (register state, no DMA).
- Effort ~3-4.5 eng-weeks, Phase E AFTER console/storage/net + post-genunix-link
  (RVV is only needed by vectorized userland: libc mem/str variants, BLAS, ML).
  solnix-FIRST: illumos gets RVV via solnix.

NEW GAPS root-caused + fixed in driver (sparc-lib-xbuild.sh):
  * NOTE(sparc-deps): SPARC_DEPS="<store-path>..." env now injects
    -I<dep>/include -L<dep>/lib -Wl,-rpath-link,<dep>/lib into configure env
    (so its link-tests resolve) + make CPPFLAGS/LDFLAGS. Fixes consuming an
    already-built sparcv9 lib that lives in the nix store, not the sysroot
    (curl needs c-ares, libarchive/libmng want bzip2/lcms2/jpeg). Was: configure
    link-test `-lcares` -> "cannot find -lcares".
  * NOTE(solaris-mimpure-text): curl's configure appends the Solaris NATIVE-ld
    flag -mimpure-text to the shared link; GNU gcc/ld reject it. Now stripped
    from every generated Makefile post-configure (safe: GNU ld allows writable
    text relocs by default).
  * NOTE(libtool-regen2) — the deep one: libtool_fix flips
    build_libtool_libs=no->yes + fills the empty per-tag archive_cmds with a
    GNU-ld -shared recipe, BUT on the FIRST `make` of a fresh tree automake's
    all-recursive re-runs config.status, which REGENERATES libtool back to
    build_libtool_libs=no BEFORE any object compiles -> objects come out non-PIC
    (pic_object=none) -> the shared link silently falls back to static-only.
    (curl shipped only libcurl.a for six rebuilds until traced.) Fix: two-phase
    build — phase-1 make settles config.status, re-apply libtool_fix, drop the
    non-PIC .o/.lo, phase-2 make now compiles PIC and links the real .so. Also
    made libtool_fix patch ALL archive_cmds="" (was count=1 template-only).
    Earlier waves' libs escaped only because their trees had no stale-Makefile
    trigger.

BLOCKED / skipped (noted why):
  * libssh2 — needs a crypto backend (openssl/mbedtls/libgcrypt/wincng); none
    is sparcv9-built yet. Blocked until a crypto lib lands.
  * brotli — upstream ships CMake only (no ./configure); this autotools driver
    can't drive it. Needs a cmake cross-toolchain-file path (out of scope).
  * curl TLS — openssl not sparcv9-built, so libcurl is c-ares+zlib, no HTTPS.
    Full TLS curl once openssl is cross-built.
  * tiff/libarchive C++ wrappers (libtiffxx, bsdtar/bsdcat) — cross cc has no
    libstdc++; disabled --disable-cxx / built the C library .so only (the
    publishable artifact).

(games + LLM hosting), and ultimately System76 COSMIC packages for solnix. Queued
research agent b7be989e -> docs/desktop-gpu-research.md (grounded, phased). Added to
Phase 3 breadth desktop track. Preliminary honest read (pending agent evidence):
- Best desktop today = OI Hipster (ships MATE, GTK3, SW-rendered Xorg via mesa
  llvmpipe). Tribblix has XFCE/MATE spins. OmniOS/SmartOS = server-only.
- Wayland on illumos = essentially NONE/experimental — blocker is the input+display
  substrate (libinput/evdev + DRM/KMS); illumos has Xorg but not the modern KMS stack
  Wayland compositors assume.
- GPU/CUDA = the HARD gap. Likely SW-render only (mesa llvmpipe); no modern DRM/KMS
  hw drivers; NVIDIA/CUDA on Solaris dropped ~2013. LLM = CPU-inference (llama.cpp)
  realistic; GPU compute NOT for foreseeable future. Games = SW OpenGL only.
- COSMIC (Rust/smithay/wgpu) = aspirational until the Wayland substrate (libinput/
  DRM-KMS) lands; a SW-rendered COSMIC MIGHT be possible after that, slow. Phased:
  P-D1 X11+mesa-SW+MATE/XFCE (feasible now, mine OI recipes) -> P-D2 Wayland substrate
  (hard, kernel input/DRM work) -> P-D3 SW compositor -> P-D4 COSMIC.

NEW GAPS FOUND + FIXED (root-caused in driver / cc, NOTE-tagged):
  * NOTE(sparc-deps-pkgconfig) [driver]: SPARC_DEPS put dep headers/.so on -I/-L
    but NOT on PKG_CONFIG_PATH. Libs that locate deps via pkg-config (fontconfig)
    saw "No package 'freetype2' found" though freetype2.pc was right there.
    Fix: add each dep's lib/pkgconfig to PKG_CONFIG_PATH.
  * NOTE(install-relink-retry) [driver]: the two-phase build (NOTE(libtool-regen2))
    leaves partial libtool state so the FIRST `make install` trips libtool's
    install-mode relink and errors EVEN THOUGH the .so was built correctly (hit by
    libgcrypt, libidn, libmd). Fix: retry `make install` once into a fresh
    $work/dest2. Proven on 3 libs.
  * FATAL-on-empty [driver]: verify step used to only WARN "no shared lib found"
    then still nix-add + let me publish an EMPTY artifact (I did publish an empty
    libmd once — see orphan note). Fix: exit 5 if no .so in dest; never publish empty.
  * NOTE(abs-work) [driver]: relative WORK= made `$work` relative, so
    `-include $work/.solaris-environ.h` was unresolvable when make ran in a
    recursive subdir (libatomic_ops: "fatal error .solaris-environ.h: No such
    file"). Fix: absolutize $work after mkdir/cd.
  * NOTE(pthread-flag) [cc]: the freestanding sparc64-none-elf gcc has no
    `-pthread` driver flag ("unrecognized command-line option '-pthread'"; hit by
    libmaxminddb). On Solaris pthreads live in libc, so `-pthread` is a safe no-op.
    Fix: strip `-pthread` from args in the cc wrapper (both compile + link).

ORPHAN (self-corrected): libmd was FIRST published EMPTY
(25fcjhqm2zdwyricvqdnavqysw0k86qh) before the FATAL-on-empty + fresh-dest fixes
landed; that narinfo is orphaned (no cached-paths row points at it). The COUNTED
libmd is the real j5101gny... with a verified libmd.so.0.1.0. Live sparcv9
manifest count is 56 = 43 prior + 12 real + 1 orphan.

  * openssl / gnutls — harder (custom Configure / p11-kit dep); task said skip if

  * json-c (-Werror calloc warning), popt (Solaris iconv const char** vs char**
