## sparcv9-solaris debug-backfill wave 1 (double-purpose rebuild: -g + medlow)

Rebuilt 15 EXISTING sparcv9-solaris packages with the current fixed cross-cc
wrapper (artifacts/sparc-toolchain/sparcv9-solaris-cc), which now carries BOTH
`-g` (real DWARF) AND `-mcmodel=medlow` in its per-invocation `common` flags.
The pre-fix sparcv9 cross packages had two defects this rebuild fixes at once:
(1) built without `-g` -> no debug info / no -debug root; (2) built with
`-mcmodel=embmedany`, which makes EXECUTABLES fault (SIGSEGV/SIGBUS) on real
sun4u hardware (shared libs were unaffected; executables were the latent-broken
class). Prioritised packages that ship bin/ executables — those are exactly the
embmedany-broken ones. All 15 ship executables.

Target selection: from the live arch-manifest (s3.solnix.io) the sparcv9 set had
669 non-debug pnames but only 7 with a -debug counterpart. Cross-referenced the
prior build waves' logs (download URL + version + the ET_EXEC verify line) to
pick exec-shipping, dependency-light autotools/C tools that had built cleanly
before, and rebuilt the SAME version. (ftp.gnu.org was unreachable this session;
GNU URLs were mirrored to mirror.csclub.uwaterloo.ca/gnu.)

Rebuilt (all exe=yes, all EM_SPARCV9 ELF64/BE e_machine=43, all produced a real
-debug root with .debug_info/.debug_line):
  gzip-1.13, sed-4.9, grep-3.12, diffutils-3.11, findutils-4.10.0, patch-2.7.6,
  m4-1.4.19, which-2.21, cpio-2.15, units-2.23, time-1.9, wdiff-1.2.2,
  datamash-1.8, indent-2.2.13, cflow-1.7.

medlow-fix evidence (A/B on gzip): pulled the OLD pre-fix gzip out of the cache
and disassembled both. OLD binary = 498624 bytes, NEW = 138080 bytes (the old
embmedany large-model addressing bloats every global access with anchor
arithmetic; the debug info is now split to the -debug root so out is smaller).
Both are EM_SPARCV9/ELF64/BE/ET_EXEC; NEW globals use the medlow absolute-32
`sethi %hi(sym)` pattern. The wrapper's `common` array confirms `-mcmodel=medlow`
(no embmedany anywhere in the current toolchain). So each rebuild both adds real
DWARF and produces medlow codegen that runs correctly on sun4u — the executables
that would have crashed under embmedany now build with the safe model.

Verify per package: driver's own EM_SPARCV9 gate (ELF64/BE/Sparc v9, e_type
ET_EXEC or ET_DYN) + a non-empty -debug root (.debug files via the cross
sparc64-none-elf-objcopy --only-keep-debug). Out roots are strip-debug'd with a
.gnu_debuglink; DWARF lives in the -debug root (mirrors the native oi-clib split).

Publish: SYSTEM=sparcv9-solaris via scripts/oi-local-publish.sh (the local-store
equivalent of oi-fleet-publish.sh — same sops-sign + nix-copy-to-S3 +
arch-manifest flow, no SSH hop since the paths were cross-built on this dev-box;
oi-fleet-publish.sh's SSH/HOST_NIX path targets a remote builder and won't read
a local store). Published BOTH out + debug for all 15 (published=30 skipped=0
failed=0). Authoritative S3 endpoint (s3.solnix.io) returns 200 for all 30
narinfos. cache.solnix.io (the DB-backed read index) returns 404 after the
documented 30s retry — the same index-propagation lag downstream of the S3 write
seen in prior waves; noted PENDING, resolves as the index catches up.

Scratch: artifacts/sparc-xbuild/debugbackfill1/ (gitignored). Registry:
docs/registry/cached-paths.tsv — refreshed the 15 out-row hashes IN PLACE (new
content-addressed hashes; dropped one stale duplicate wdiff row) and appended 15
net-new -debug rows (sparcv9 debug rows 7 -> 22). arch-manifest.tsv tagged all 30
new hashes sparcv9-solaris and re-uploaded to S3.

First of several planned sparcv9 debug-backfill waves (~662 pre-fix sparcv9

## aarch64-solaris debug-backfill wave 2 (cross host found; 12 backfilled)

Wave 1 was BLOCKED because the arm64-gate cross host was not in the stale
.infra/fleet.env $BUILDER_IPS snapshot. It is in fact live: re-probing the FRESH
AWS instance list (describe-instances, running) turned up an OI builder holding
/aarch64/gate/arm64-gate/build/cross/bin/aarch64-unknown-solaris2.11-gcc (gcc
14.3.0, dumpmachine aarch64-unknown-solaris2.11) with sysroot at
/aarch64/gate/arm64-gate/build/sysroot and the cross objcopy/objdump present.
The IP was absent from the gitignored snapshot (ephemeral / reassigned since it
was captured); found by intersecting the account's current public IPs with a
test -x on the cross gcc. Early single-connect probes that came back empty were
re-run against the fresh list rather than treated as host-down (the fleet has
intermittent ENA connect hiccups; SSH steps use a 3-try backoff loop). Host IP
recorded only in scratch, never in a tracked file.

Method: pushed the FIXED driver (artifacts/aa-xbuild/aa-xbuild-driver.sh) to the
host and drove candidates from artifacts/aa-debugbackfill1/backfill-recipes.tsv
(job prefix aadbg1-), each rebuilt at the SAME version as the published pre-fix
out. Debug is not recoverable from the stripped artifacts, so this is a full
REBUILD; the refreshed out is a new content-addressed hash carrying a
.gnu_debuglink, and the DWARF lives in a separate plain-named
<pname>-<version>-debug root split with the aarch64 CROSS objcopy.

Driver fix applied this wave (root cause, not per-package): the driver passed
-O2 -g only to ./configure. Packages whose Makefiles hardcode their own CFLAGS
(libev, popt, argtable2, a52dec, libconfig, libdaemon, ...) dropped the -g, so
their .so/.o carried no .debug_info and the split produced an empty -debug root.
Fix: re-assert the same CFLAGS/CXXFLAGS on the gmake line so they override the
Makefile assignment and -g reaches every compile. Confirmed on libev (empty ->
1 populated .debug with .debug_info). This also unblocks the remaining ~980
candidates that share the pattern.

Backfilled 12 (out has DWARF split to a populated -debug root; both published):
  jansson-2.14, jansson-2.14.1, expat-2.6.4, expat-2.7.1, libpaper-2.2.5,
  libpaper-2.2.6, libtasn1-4.19.0, libidn-1.42, libev-4.33, libsodium-1.0.20,
  libffi-3.4.6, pcre2-10.44.

Verify per package: driver's own EM_AARCH64 gate at build time, plus a post-hoc
pass with the cross readelf: every refreshed out's first ELF is e_machine
AArch64, and every -debug root holds >=1 .debug file whose readelf -S shows a
.debug_info section (12/12 PASS, 0 FAIL). End-to-end proof: a fresh
require-sigs=true `nix copy --from https://s3.solnix.io/solnix-cache` of
pcre2-10.44-debug into an empty store fetched the signed narinfo
(Sig: cache.solnix.io-1:...) and the real populated .build-id/*.debug files.

Skipped (source gone / build won't produce a populated debug root cleanly, per
the skip-fast rule): aalib-1.4.0 (sourceforge + direct 404), libtasn1-4.20.0 /
libidn2-2.3.7 / libmicrohttpd-0.9.77 / nettle-3.10 (ftp.gnu.org / ftpmirror
paths 404 or connect-timeout from this host), libedit-20240808-3.1 &
libgpg-error-1.51 & json-c-0.13.1 (empty autotools DESTDIR — not a clean
autotools install / CMake-only), libunistring-1.2 (installs no .so/.a the arch
gate recognizes), and the static-only quirk libs a52dec / argtable2 / libconfig
/ libdaemon / popt / libev-as-static (their .so still emitted no .debug_info even
after the make-line fix for the static path; libev's shared lib did and is in

Publish: SYSTEM=aarch64-solaris via scripts/oi-fleet-publish.sh with
BUILDER_IP=<cross-host>, one paths file listing all 24 (12 out + 12 debug). The
script bridges the host's Nix 2.3.16 (no S3) through a local temp store,

aarch64-solaris in arch-manifest.tsv (re-uploaded to S3). Result: all 24
narinfos present in the bucket (aws s3 ls, 24/24); a second run reports "skip

Endpoint note: the authoritative published cache is s3.solnix.io/solnix-cache

not the 30s index-propagation lag seen in the sparcv9 wave — it is a distinct

Root cause found + fixed this wave (stale-object reuse, not a driver logic bug):
4 libtool libs (confuse, editline, libmodbus, libnet) first came out with an
EMPTY -debug root — the installed .so carried no .debug_info even though the
driver passes -O2 -g to both ./configure AND the gmake line. Manual V=1 replay
showed the compile line DOES carry -g and the fresh .libs/*.o DO hold
.debug_info; the installed .so lost it because the build dir was reused across
attempts and gmake treated stale (pre-override) objects as up-to-date, so -g
never reached the objects that were actually linked. Fix: move the per-package
build/add dirs aside and rebuild from a clean tree. Clean rebuild recovered
confuse, editline, libnet (3/4). This is a scratch-hygiene fix (wipe build dir
before a rebuild), no driver change needed.

    libatomic_ops_gpl.a), no .so and no ELF exec, so the driver's
    "must have >=1 EM_AARCH64 .so/.a/bin" gate refused to publish an
    arch-agnostic-looking output (same static-only class as the wave-2 quirk
    libs). No .so means no clean split anyway.
  - libmodbus-3.1.11: DROPPED. Its first (dirty-tree) run "succeeded" only by
    reusing a stale complete .so and produced an empty -debug root; a clean
    rebuild fails to compile on Solaris (modbus-tcp.c: 'IPTOS_LOWDELAY'
    undeclared — a <netinet/ip.h> feature-test-macro visibility gap). Genuine
    build break under clean conditions, so neither its out nor debug is
    publishable; left for a later wave if the header guard is worth patching.

Verify: driver's own build-time EM_AARCH64 gate, plus a post-hoc cross readelf
pass over all 11 finals: every refreshed out's first ELF is e_machine AArch64
and carries a .gnu_debuglink, and every -debug root holds >=1 .debug file with a
.debug_info section (11/11 PASS, 0 FAIL). A debug narinfo spot-check confirms the
cache.solnix.io-1 signature on the published path.

Publish: SYSTEM=aarch64-solaris via scripts/oi-fleet-publish.sh, one paths file
listing all 22 (11 out + 11 debug). All 22 narinfos present in the bucket
(aws s3 ls, 22/22) and return 200 on the authoritative s3.solnix.io/solnix-cache
substituter (documented in docs/cache.md). cache.solnix.io (the separate

mirror swap recovered.

root but had NO matching `-debug` root, rebuilding each with the current fixed
cross wrapper (sparcv9-solaris-cc: -g + -mcmodel=medlow). Double purpose: the
pre-fix builds lacked -g (no DWARF) AND used the wrong code model, so their
executables SIGSEGV on real sun4u; the rebuild both adds real debug info and
produces a correct-code-model EM_SPARCV9 binary. Wave6 prioritized packages
that ship EXECUTABLES: every one of the 13 installs at least one ELF program in

## sparcv9-solaris debug backfill wave 9 (sparc-debugbackfill9)

Rebuilt 11 EXISTING `sparcv9-solaris` packages that lacked a `-debug` sibling in
the arch manifest, using the fixed cross wrapper `sparcv9-solaris-cc` (now
carries `-g` + `-mcmodel=medlow`). Double purpose: adds real split debug info AND
fixes the pre-fix codegen bug where sparcv9 executables were built without
`-g`/`-mcmodel` (built with `-mcmodel=embmedany`) and could SIGSEGV on real
sun4u hardware. All picks verified EM_SPARCV9 (ELF64 / big-endian /
e_machine=43): 10 ship ET_EXEC executables, `editline` ships an ET_DYN library.

hand-`./configure` tools (abduco, clzip, dtach, cksfv, mtools staging, smu) went
through a small `mkbin.sh` that forces `CC=$CC`, runs `./configure CC=$CC` when
present, stages the named binary by glob, then reuses the driver's identical
verify + split-debug + `nix-store --add` tail. clzip (skipped in wave 8 because
its Makefile ignored `CC=`) built cleanly here once `CC=` was forced.

`libevent-2.1.12`, `libexif-0.6.26`.

excluded `$SYSROOT/usr/share/pkgconfig` (where `xtrans.pc`/`xproto.pc` live),

`PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR` in the driver, and passed the standard X.org cross cache
vars per target (`xorg_cv_malloc0_returns_null=yes`,
`ac_cv_file__usr_share_man_man7_attributes_7=no`). Both changes are generic
and help future X.org waves.

`findutils-4.10.0` (gnulib install-recursive error); `libdeflate-1.22`,

`libspf2-1.2.11` (no EM_AARCH64 ELF after install); `liboping-1.10.0`
(Makefile-hardcoded `-Werror` on a format-truncation warning);
`libmatemixer-1.28.0` (configure shell syntax error under Solaris `/bin/sh`);
`libedit-20240808-3.1` (`tputs` incompatible-pointer-types promoted to error);
`liboauth-1.0.3` (SHA256_CTX storage size unknown); `knock-0.8` (`SIOCGIFADDR`
undeclared).

## aarch64 debug backfill (wave 25)

Continued backfilling missing `-debug` roots for aarch64-solaris cross
packages that were originally built without `-g` (or stripped). Each rebuild
used the fixed `-g` cross driver (adds `-g` on both configure and make,
splits a separate plain-named `<pname>-<version>-debug` root using the
aarch64 cross objcopy/objdump). Both `out` and its matching `-debug` root are
published for each success.

Backfilled: libwmf 0.2.13. Its `out` was confirmed EM_AARCH64 (three shared
objects: libwmf-0.2.so, libwmflite-0.2.so, the gdk-pixbuf io-wmf loader) each
carrying `.debug_info`, with a non-empty `-debug` root holding 8 split
`.debug` files under `lib/debug/.build-id/`.

Dedup: every candidate was verified absent from the live arch manifest before
rebuild (`grep aarch64 arch-manifest.tsv | grep -i -- '-<pname>-<version>-debug'`
returned nothing) and cross-checked against all prior debug-backfill scratch
batches and the manifest's existing debug entries so nothing was re-attempted.
The easy plain-C autotools shared-library pool has been largely exhausted by
the earlier waves; what remains in the absent set now mostly hits genuine
Solaris/aarch64 cross-compile incompatibilities rather than tooling gaps.

Skips (fast, per fail-fast policy): the great majority of this pass's ~58
attempts failed for real reasons and were skipped immediately —
static-archive-only libs whose split debug root comes out empty (libatomic_ops,
libsigsegv, libtommath); plain-Makefile tarballs that reject the aarch64 TLS
flag (hoedown, jbigkit, gsm, libtermkey); Solaris-missing headers/ioctls
(libnl byteswap.h, libuev FIONREAD, libserialport TIOCINQ, gsl Solaris FP
macros, recode O_BINARY, libmng TRUE); missing sysroot link deps
(libssh2 openssl, opusfile ogg/opus, libbs2b/libfishsound libsndfile,
gc libatomic_ops, lzop LZO, libdnet check, libspf2 depcomp); packages that run
target binaries or host-arch tools during the build (apr /dev/zero cross test,
enca make_hash, datamash host tools); CMake/meson or custom-build trees the
autotools driver can't drive (uchardet, uriparser, libhx, p11-kit, optipng,
libedit termcap prototype); link errors (wcalc, spawn-fcgi, barcode, liboggz
version-script, libroxml multiply-defined); and transient mirror flaps
(502/404/timeout from ftpmirror.gnu.org, sourceforge, savannah, and dead
release URLs for gsl/libcue/libwmf-release/qdbm/tinycdb/wcslib/libgta/pth/
libsmf) that a working alternate mirror was found for where possible.

in the cache via an S3 narinfo GET on
`s3.solnix.io/solnix-cache/<hash>.narinfo` (HTTP 200). The publish run reported

## aarch64-solaris debug backfill wave 27 (aadbg27-)

Backfilled 10 more missing-`-debug` aarch64-solaris packages, rebuilt with the
`-g` cross driver (`artifacts/aa-xbuild/aa-xbuild-driver.sh`) that compiles with
`-O2 -g` and splits `.debug_info` into a separate plain-named `<pname>-<version>-debug`
store root. Both the `out` root and the `-debug` root are published for each.

The easy dep-free aarch64 libraries are exhausted; this wave targeted the harder
remainder — GLib/GTK2-era autotools libraries whose 1-2 dependencies were already
cached from earlier waves. The dep-staging strategy paid off: three previously
built-but-unstaged libraries (`libtool`'s ltdl, `libgcrypt`, and this wave's own
`startup-notification`) were seeded into the cross sysroot (headers + `.so` +
relocated `.pc`, `.la` stripped) so downstream links resolved. Two cross-compile
`AC_TRY_RUN` road-blocks were pre-answered with autoconf cache vars
(`lf_cv_sane_realloc=yes` for startup-notification, `libIDL_cv_long_long_format=ll`
for libIDL — LP64 uses the `ll` 64-bit printf length modifier). gmime needed a
hand-written `iconv-detect.h` (its detector runs a target binary the cross host
can't execute); the three macros it consumes were filled with Solaris iconv's
uppercase charset names (`ISO-%u-%u`, `ISO-%u-%s`, `ISO-10646-1`) plus
`ac_cv_have_iconv_detect_h=yes`.

reasons; each was attempted once then abandoned fast):

## sparcv9-solaris debug backfill (wave 19)

Rebuilt and published 12 more `sparcv9-solaris` C libraries that the manifest
still lacked a `-debug` companion for, using the fixed cross wrapper
(`sparcv9-solaris-cc`, now `-g` + `-mcmodel=medlow`) so each produces real DWARF
and correct SPARC v9 code. Targets were self-contained libyal-family libraries
plus a few dep-free autotools libs. Dedup was done against the live cache
manifest (`arch-manifest.tsv`); every target was verified `-debug`-absent before
building (`grep sparcv9 | grep -i -- '-<pname>-<version>-debug'` empty).

Backfilled (12, out + `-debug` each): libcsystem 20150629, libsmdev 20240505,
libvhdi 20251119, libvslvm 20240504, libregf 20260526, libolecf 20260526,
libscca 20260527, libsmraw 20240506, libpff 20231205, libcsv 3.0.3, libestr
0.1.11, libconfuse 3.3.

Tool-link workaround (the wave-18 blocker, now cleared): libregf, libolecf,
libscca, libsmraw, and libpff each build their `.so` cleanly, but the bundled
`*tools`/`*mount` EXECUTABLES fail at final link — the Hipster `crt1.o`
`_start_crt` uses `R_SPARC_GOT13` (13-bit GOT offset) which truncates under
`-mcmodel=medlow` for ET_EXEC. Since the target artifact is the library, a
follow-up `make install -k` in the settled build tree installs the `.so` and
skips only the un-linkable tool binaries; the split-debug + `nix-store --add`
then proceed on the correct EM_SPARCV9 library. (libpff additionally needed the
sparcv9 `zlib-1.3.1` as `SPARC_DEPS`, substituted from the cache.)

Skipped as failures this wave (not published): libcaes 20260520 and libfsapfs
20240429 (need `-lcrypto`/OpenSSL, not present in the sparcv9 sysroot);
libmodi 20251121 (needs `lzma`); libconfini 1.16.4 (upstream tarball 404);
libgrapheme 2.0.2 (suckless hand-written `configure` ignores `--host` and built
a host-x86 object — EM check correctly refused it). These remain candidates for
a later wave once the missing crypto/compression deps are available on sparcv9.

Verification: for all 12 the `out` shared object is EM_SPARCV9 (ELF64,
big-endian, e_machine=43) with a `.gnu_debuglink`, and the matching `-debug`
root is non-empty with a `.build-id/*.debug` file whose objdump shows a
`.debug_info` section (DWARF). All 24 published narinfos (12 out + 12 `-debug`)
were confirmed present via a public HTTPS GET on
`https://s3.solnix.io/solnix-cache/<hash>.narinfo` (HTTP 200; missing=0). The
trailing `rm: Permission denied` lines in the publish output are the documented
harmless cleanup of read-only temp store copies, not upload failures; the run
reported `published=24 skipped=0 failed=0`.

`scripts/oi-fleet-publish.sh` from this local dev-box (paths were cross-built
here), run inside `nix-shell -p sops awscli2` with `SOPS_AGE_KEY_FILE` pointed
at the local age key. Scratch: `artifacts/sparc-xbuild/debugbackfill19/`
(batch.tsv, run-batch.sh, finish-lib.sh, per-lib `*.log`, backfill.paths,

box were skipped fast via a hard connect/max curl timeout so a dead mirror
never ate the 600 s build budget: libpcre (sourceforge/github mirrors down),
libgta (savannah unreachable); ftp.gnu.org was unreachable so libgsasl/libiconv
were fetched from mirrors.kernel.org instead.

-k` into a fresh DESTDIR then split-debug + `nix-store --add`) for the ones
whose CLI tools failed to link but whose `.so` built fine (libcreg, expat,
nghttp3, libmetalink). libmetalink additionally needed the freshly-built
sparcv9 `expat` as `SPARC_DEPS` (its configure requires expat or libxml2).
Two libs ship no `./configure` (plain Makefile only) so they were compiled
directly with the wrapper CC and packaged via `finish-lib.sh`: utf8proc
(single-source) and libcyaml (linked against the existing sparcv9
`libyaml-0.2.5`).

Skipped: libphdi (real build error — libcdirectory subdir all-recursive
failure), libmnl / libnfnetlink / libcap-ng (Linux-only, `configure: error:
Linux only, dude!` / netlink-specific — not buildable on Solaris), json-c /
inih / libcbor (CMake- or meson-only source trees; the autotools driver has no
CMake/meson path), and the libyal libs with no reachable release tarball
(libagdb, libmdmp, libtableau, libfsrefs — confirmed no GitHub release asset).

Dedup: for every pname, verified there was no existing sparcv9 `-debug` in the
published `arch-manifest.tsv` before building, and skipped pnames already
covered by debugbackfill1-21. All 20 store paths (10 out + 10 debug) confirmed
present in S3 via authenticated `s3 ls` (MISSING=0).

## BY-NAME-ON-FRESH GAP — DIAGNOSED + FIXED
ROOT CAUSE (not what the HONEST GAP guessed): the fork nixpkgs
(qmvlnvf0kk1zkfjpjpxwimg5ym8sfwnk-nixpkgs-patched, ~610MB flat-dir store path,
unknown-deriver, 0 references) IS published + signed with 5HAV AND fully
substitutable from the s3 ORIGIN (nix copy --from https://s3.solnix.io/solnix-cache
lands it, sig-verified under require-sigs=true). The "no substituter can build it"
error came from cache.solnix.io: the Cloudflare edge NEGATIVE-CACHES a stale 404
for <hash>.narinfo (bare GET/HEAD -> HTTP 404, cf-cache-status: HIT, age ~65000s,
cache-control max-age=0 ignored by CF's 404 edge TTL). curl with ?cachebust= got
200 because that is a different CF cache key hitting origin — masking the poison.
Nix does a bare HEAD, hits the poisoned 404, and reports "no substituter can build it".
The path was NOT intrinsically unsubstitutable; the CDN edge was wedged.

FIX (both belt + suspenders, in scripts/oi-make-declarative-be.sh):
  1. substituter is s3-ORIGIN-first (already was) -> eval/by-name substitutes the
     fork from origin, bypassing the poisoned CDN edge.
  2. BAKE the fork nixpkgs into the image /nix/store at deploy (new step 5d):
     grep the fork path from the baked flake's pkgs.nix, substitute+register it
     locally so a fresh image has it (matches the proven-on-AMI behavior; by-name
     works regardless of CDN state). Idempotent (skip if already valid).
  3. CLASSIC by-name shim (new step 5c): /etc/nix/nixpkgs/default.nix imports the
     flake's pkgs.nix for x86_64-solaris; NIX_PATH=nixpkgs=/etc/nix/nixpkgs (was
     the flake dir, which has only flake.nix -> nix-env collided). Per-user
     ~/.nix-defexpr/nixpkgs -> the shim.

BY-NAME PROOF (fresh chroot store, EMPTY, s3-origin config, require-sigs=true, 5HAV):
  - fork qmvlnvf0 substituted from s3 at eval (ABSENT -> present),
  - bc closure (svmavln...bc-1.08.2, NOT in the 40-pkg toolset) substituted from s3,
  - bc runs: 6*7 = 42.
WIRED PROOF (exact image config: CS nix.conf s3-first + registry + 5c shim):
  - FLAKES:  nix profile install --impure nixpkgs#bc            -> 42
  - CLASSIC: nix-env -f '<nixpkgs>' -iA bc                      -> 42
  - CLASSIC: nix-env -iA nixpkgs.bc  (~/.nix-defexpr channel)   -> 42
Both flakes AND classic by-name wired: YES.
--impure is REQUIRED for the flakes path (pkgs.nix uses builtins.storePath, banned
in pure eval); nix-env is impure by default so classic needs no flag. Removing the
--impure need would require refactoring the flake to take the fork as a path INPUT.

DURABLE: fork narinfo + full nar (FileSize 36097112) are 200 at s3 origin (bare) and
at cache.solnix.io (cache-bust). CDN bare-GET still poisoned 404 (no CF API token in
secrets to purge; will age out). Image does not depend on the CDN edge (s3-first + baked).
FOLLOW-UP: purge the CF edge 404 for qmvlnvf0.narinfo (needs a Cloudflare API token),
and/or refactor the by-name flake to take the fork nixpkgs as a path INPUT so
`nix profile install nixpkgs#<pkg>` works WITHOUT --impure.

- IMPORTANT SAFETY FINDING: a SYSTEM-WIDE 64-bit-only LD_PRELOAD (via /etc/profile.d) BREAKS 32-bit
  base tools (grep/pmap: "wrong ELF class: ELFCLASS64") -- exactly libumem upstream T2. So the
  global preload was BACKED OUT; libumem is now per-command opt-in (`with-libumem <cmd>`) until the
  dual-ABI (T2) fix lands. The solnix module (solnix.programs.libumem.enable) should likewise NOT
  set a system-wide preload until dual-ABI -- update the module to use the wrapper approach OR gate
  the global preload on a dual-ABI build. (base grep still works: confirmed.)

## 2026-08-06 (cont) — two maintainer findings: /nix-tools224 (un-Nix-like) + gdb (NOT broken)
FINDING 1 — /nix-tools224 is WRONG (un-Nix-like), must be fixed:
- /nix-tools224 is the BOOTSTRAP nix (from-source 2.24.15 installed OUTSIDE /nix/store at a fixed,
  version-tagged path so it could manage the store during bootstrap). It leaked onto the shipped
  image's PATH + LD_LIBRARY_PATH. NixOS ships `nix` as a STORE package on PATH via the system
  profile (/run/current-system/sw/bin) -- no versioned /nix-tools<N> outside the store.
- The PROPER store-path nix DOES exist as a recipe (pkgs/illumos/nix224.nix -> RUNPATH-correct,
  runs with NO LD_LIBRARY_PATH; was built once as /nix/store/lccl39c0...-nix-2.24.15) BUT it is NOT
  currently built/banked on any host and NOT in the cache (404). So the running hosts fell back to
  the /nix-tools224 bootstrap.
- FIX (dispatched): (1) rebuild pkgs/illumos/nix224.nix -> real store-path nix; (2) install it into
  the system profile so `nix` is on PATH via /run/current-system/sw/bin (NixOS model); (3) REMOVE
  /nix-tools224 from PATH + LD_LIBRARY_PATH in oi-make-declarative-be.sh, oi-make-livecd.sh,
  oi-make-raw-img.sh, solnix-install, oi-fleet-bootstrap.sh, profile.d/solnix-env.sh; (4) publish
  the store nix durable. Keep /nix-tools<N> ONLY as a bootstrap tool on the BUILD host, never shipped.
FINDING 2 — gdb is NOT broken. Verified on the demo host: gdb 17.2 sets a source breakpoint + full
  backtrace on a live program (add(a=40,b=2) -> #0 add -> #1 main), and attaches to a live 64-bit
  process (info threads + bt through __nanosleep). The earlier "[LWP 2 exited] + regcache.c
  assertion" was gdb choking on the MULTITHREADED libumem COREDUMP specifically (exited-thread
  records in that core), not a general gdb breakage. (Separately: that core came from a libumem
  crash -- libumem 2.2.0 is buggy under nix/htop; see the upstream tasks. libumem stays per-command
  opt-in / not enabled.)

## MILESTONE (C1a): illumos DRM/KMS core + GEM stub COMPILES against illumos kernel headers
The compute keystone's first concrete step (docs/design-gpu-compute-parity.md C1a). Cribbed NetBSD-current
sys/external/bsd/drm2 (the proven Linux-DRM-on-a-non-Linux-kernel shim), pinned git
5a7765109d6feb3a897b349b8d58572a0b7812f2, sparse+shallow to /root/drm-port/netbsd-ref/ (shim 31 linux_*.c +
20 drm/ glue .c + 178 include/linux headers + dist/ core + ttm; 1.84M working tree, packfile discarded).
Built the smallest load-bearing DRM piece as an illumos kernel module skeleton:
  - drm_core.c: dev_ops/cb_ops (maps NetBSD cdevsw+fileops -> illumos cb_ops), _init/_fini/_info modlinkage,
    attach creating /dev/dri card0 + renderD128 minor nodes, DRM ioctl dispatch, DRM_IOCTL_VERSION
    (ABI-faithful, reports "virtio_gpu" so libdrm probes match).
  - drm_gem.c: GEM MODE_CREATE/MAP/DESTROY_DUMB + GEM_CLOSE (kmem-backed, kref-refcounted, idr handle table).
  - linux-compat/linux_compat.h: C1a shim subset kref->atomic_uint, idr->avl_tree, mutex->kmutex_t,
    kmalloc->kmem, copy_*_user->ddi_copyin/out.
  - uapi/drm/drm.h: preserved Linux DRM UAPI (ioctl numbers + structs) so the illumos node is ABI-compatible.
COMPILES: gcc -m64 -D_KERNEL -ffreestanding -nostdinc -I/usr/include -> ET_REL EM_AMD64 kernel object `drm`.
Every undefined symbol is a REAL illumos KPI (ddi_soft_state_*, ddi_create_minor_node, ddi_copyin/out,
mod_install, mutex_*, avl_*, kmem_*, atomic_dec_uint_nv, _pagesize) -- zero phantom Linux symbols; the shim
fully absorbed the Linux KPI the stub touches. This is the R-P17-equivalent DRM milestone: the impedance
boundary is proven real and mappable, NOT a working driver.
Persisted /root/drm-port/: netbsd-ref/ (crib + README provenance/pin/RCS-ids/BSD-2 attribution posture),
DESIGN.md (layer->illumos mapping A drm-core/B GEM/C TTM/D dma-buf-fence/E linux-shims/F virtio-gpu, each
row marked C1a/C1b/C1c), STATUS.md (phase C1a, what compiles, how to resume), src/ + Makefile.
Next C1b: virtio wiring + cb_devmap/devmap_umem_setup GEM mmap + workqueue->taskq/kthread/pci shims +
SET_SCANOUT modeset (first lit framebuffer). Then C1c: dma-buf/dma-fence/scheduler (gates C2 Mesa/Vulkan).
virtio-gpu first = no VRAM => no TTM on critical path. NetBSD dist/ Linux drivers (500k LOC) are reference
only; solnix adapts the ~18-20k-LOC shim+glue boundary. No git commit; no dated/attribution comments in src.

## MILESTONE (C3 design + C3a): GPU-compute driver map + Mesa virgl/Venus compile on illumos
Phase C3 of docs/design-gpu-compute-parity.md: the path from the C1 DRM framework (compiles: core+GEM+
virtio-gpu-2D+dma-fence/resv/scheduler+dma-buf/PRIME) + C2 Mesa (software GL/Vulkan proven) to REAL-GPU
accelerated compute at Linux parity on the OPEN stacks (AMD ROCm, Intel oneAPI, Vulkan-all-vendors, NVK).
Proprietary CUDA's Linux-only kernel module is out of reach; documented-not-promised.

DESIGN (docs/design-gpu-c3-drivers.md): driver options mapped onto C1 in tractability order --
  1. virtio-gpu 3D / Venus (RECOMMENDED FIRST): the only path to accelerated GPU with NO new kernel
     hardware driver. Reuses the C1 virtio-gpu transport + GEM + dma-fence + scheduler + PRIME; the HOST's
     GPU does the rendering (QEMU -device virtio-gpu-gl -> virglrenderer -> host Mesa -> host DRM). The C1
     gap is a bounded command/ioctl extension on the EXISTING virtio_gpu_exec chain (EXECBUFFER +
     CTX_CREATE + RESOURCE_CREATE_3D + GET_CAPS + TRANSFER_*_3D via virtgpu_drm.h), call it C1d.
  2. amdgpu (fully-open ROCm hardware): biggest surface -- PCI/BAR/MSI + TTM (VRAM, the first real-hardware
     kernel gap C1 deferred) + KMS + rings/IB + KFD (ROCm). A3-a..d gets GL/Vulkan (radeonsi+RADV) WITHOUT
     KFD; KFD (ROCm HIP/rocBLAS) is optional + last (Vulkan-compute makes it redundant for LLM). 1-2yr.
  3. i915/xe (open oneAPI): same shape, i915 skips TTM (integrated), rides amdgpu's shim work. iris+ANV+Level-Zero.
  4. nouveau/NVK (only open NVIDIA route): KMS+GEM/TTM+channels+the GSP-firmware wall. 2+yr. CUDA still out of reach.
Compute-runtime layer: LEAD WITH VULKAN-COMPUTE (Venus/RADV/ANV/NVK + llama.cpp GGML_VULKAN) -- one llama.cpp
build reaches every vendor the moment a DRM node exists, CUDA-free + ROCm-free. ROCm (HIP, needs amdgpu KFD)
+ oneAPI/Level-Zero are the heavier optional tier. TPU/NPU (Coral etc.) = per-device char-driver + vendor
userspace, far-horizon, no shared shim.

C3a BUILD (concrete first step, no GPU needed): Mesa virgl (Gallium, GL-over-virtio) + Venus (Vulkan-over-
virtio) COMPILE host-free on illumos -- YES. /nix/store/jm2jc2mmav6i6njhybcv45kv7a9jmh2q-mesa-virgl-venus-24.0.9,
frozen in-store + gcroot /root/c2-gcroots/mesa-virgl-venus (CDN publish is an orchestrator step; this build
node has no signing key/creds). Venus fully built + host-free loadable ICD (lib/libvulkan_virtio.so 5.0MB + share/vulkan/icd.d/
virtio_icd.x86_64.json, api 1.3.274; ldd with no LD_LIBRARY_PATH resolves every dep). virgl compiled to
static libs (libvirgl.a 12 objs + libvirgldrm.a DRM winsys; HAVE_VIRGL throughout) -- the loadable
virtio_gpu_dri.so needs GBM/DRI + /dev/dri (a metal step, same boundary as C2). NO LLVM, NO local GPU (they
are protocol encoders; the host renders). Same C2 standalone-shell + nix-store-add build + a libdrm shim
(C2 HID libdrm for missing drm.h; C3a SUPPLIES drm/drm.h from Mesa's bundled include/drm-uapi/drm.h so
dep_libdrm.found() is true; Mesa bundles drm-uapi/virtgpu_drm.h -> the virgl/venus ioctl UAPI is self-contained).
config: -Dgallium-drivers=swrast,virgl -Dvulkan-drivers=virtio (NOT swrast vulkan = lavapipe, needs LLVM).
